title: The Transformation of Oncology Drug Development in China: Toward a New Phase of Innovation.
authors: Chen Y, Liu D, Song Y et al.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: China's oncology drug development ecosystem has shifted from rapid pipeline expansion toward clinical value-driven innovation. We review regulatory reform and the 2015 to 2025 evolution of clinical development across small molecules, mAbs, multispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and cell and gene therapies. China's disease burden and enrollment capacity have enabled globally relevant advances in EGFR-mutant lung cancer, gastrointestinal malignancies, hepatocellular carcinoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and CLDN18.2-directed therapies. We highlight persistent challenges in target and modality convergence, biomarker definition, therapeutic window optimization, manufacturing consistency, and globally interpretable evidence generation and discuss how artificial intelligence may connect target discovery, drug design, and clinical trial optimization more efficiently.
SIGNIFICANCE: China has become a major source of oncology trials and modality innovation, but scale alone will not ensure global impact. This review links regulatory reform, disease-specific opportunity, target biology, therapeutic format, and evidence quality across a decade of solid tumor development. It defines the conditions under which China-originated programs can generate globally practice-changing evidence. See related article by Shi, p. XX .

title: Molecular Profiling and Precision Oncology for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer in Latin America: Unique Epidemiology, Persistent Barriers, and Paths Toward Equity.
authors: Picón CR, Borea R, Rizzo MM et al.
abstract: ABSTRACT: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) represents a critical public health crisis in Latin America (LA), the leading cause of cancer-associated mortality across the region. Although global incidence rates are shifting, the burden in low- and middle-income countries is projected to increase significantly by 2030. Beyond the impact of tobacco, LA faces unique challenges derived from environmental exposures and diverse genetic ancestry that shape a molecular landscape distinct from other regions. This has resulted in a high prevalence of actionable drivers, particularly EGFR mutations, positioning a large segment of the population as ideal candidates for precision medicine approaches. However, current efforts to address this epidemic fall short of regional needs, as the potential of precision oncology remains largely unrealized due to multilevel systemic and economic barriers. Despite the scientific potential of targeted therapies to drastically improve survival, LA has not broadly or expeditiously adopted these strategies. A profound implementation gap is characterized by a reliance on inefficient single-gene testing, fragmented regulatory frameworks, and severe infrastructural limitations. Consequently, only a minimal proportion of the regional patient population benefits from recent advances, whereas the majority continue to receive empirical chemotherapy with significantly inferior survival outcomes. Addressing these disparities requires a steadfast focus on systemic transformation, ranging from establishing centralized genomic hubs to implementing structured educational programs. Standardizing care through molecular tumor boards (MTBs) and harmonizing regulatory pathways are essential steps in translating research into clinical benefits. In this review, we discuss the unique molecular epidemiology of the region and the challenges of treatment implementation, focusing on the urgent need to integrate new technologies to ensure equitable access to precision oncology. LA has one of the highest potential population-level benefits from precision oncology in NSCLC; however, systemic barriers prevent this molecular opportunity from translating into equitable survival gains (Graphical abstract).

title: Association between adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy and survival outcomes in completely resected stage I invasive lung adenocarcinoma (≤3 cm) with sensitizing EGFR mutations and pathological high-risk features.
authors: Cao J, Huang Z, Qiu F et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adjuvant epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy improves prognosis in patients with resected EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer. However, evidence supporting its use in stage I disease with pathological high-risk features remains limited. We evaluated the association between adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy and survival outcomes in patients with completely resected stage I invasive lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) (≤3 cm), sensitizing EGFR mutations, and pathological high-risk features.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent complete resection for stage I invasive LUAD (≤3 cm) between January 2011 and May 2024. Eligible patients had an EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R mutation and at least one pathological high-risk feature, including lymphovascular invasion, visceral pleural invasion, spread through air spaces, high-grade histologic patterns (micropapillary, solid, and complex glandular patterns), or poor differentiation. The study outcomes were relapse-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS). The primary analysis used a 90-day landmark design, with baseline differences addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). Survival distributions were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Simon-Makuch curves and time-dependent Cox regression analysis were additionally used to account for changes in treatment exposure over time. A 120-day landmark analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis.
RESULTS: Among 357 eligible patients, 354 remained alive and relapse-free at the 90-day landmark. Of these, 104 had initiated adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy by the landmark, whereas 250 had not. In the unweighted landmark analysis, adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy was associated with improved RFS (P=0.004; HR =0.27, 95% CI: 0.13-0.56). This association remained significant after IPTW adjustment (P=0.009; HR =0.28, 95% CI: 0.11-0.68). No significant difference in OS was observed in either the unweighted analysis (P=0.91; HR =0.93, 95% CI: 0.33-2.63) or the IPTW-weighted analysis (P=0.38; HR =1.34, 95% CI: 0.50-3.61). In the time-dependent analysis, EGFR-TKI exposure was associated with a lower hazard of relapse (P<0.001; HR =0.27, 95% CI: 0.14-0.52) but not with OS (P=0.49; HR =1.14, 95% CI: 0.41-3.19). The 120-day landmark sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with completely resected stage I invasive LUAD (≤3 cm), sensitizing EGFR mutations, and pathological high-risk features, adjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy was associated with improved RFS, whereas no significant association with OS was observed.

title: Diagnostic challenge of delayed immune-related hepatitis during zongertinib treatment after nivolumab plus ipilimumab in a 52-year-old man with HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a case report.
authors: Oba T, Shiohira S, Machida Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Delayed immune-related hepatitis after discontinuation of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is increasingly recognized, but attribution is difficult when liver injury develops during subsequent tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This diagnostic dilemma has not been well described during human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-selective TKI treatment after dual ICI therapy.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 52-year-old Japanese man with HER2 exon 20 insertion-positive stage IVB non-small cell lung cancer received nivolumab plus ipilimumab from February 28 to November 13, 2025, and developed grade 2 oral mucositis, grade 2 adrenal insufficiency, and grade 1-2 skin toxicity. Zongertinib was initiated on November 26. Routine testing on January 6, 2026 showed grade 3 hepatocellular injury, and zongertinib was withheld. Despite drug withdrawal, liver injury progressed, and he was admitted with mild fatigue on January 20, when aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and γ-glutamyl transpeptidase levels were 774, 1,386, 156, and 160 U/L, respectively. Total bilirubin remained approximately 1.0 mg/dL. Viral and autoimmune testing and imaging disclosed no alternative cause. Liver biopsy showed active hepatitis with lymphocyte-predominant portal and lobular inflammation and interface activity, findings compatible with an immune-mediated hepatitis pattern but not specific for the causative agent. Prednisolone 40 mg/day (approximately 0.5 mg/kg/day) produced rapid biochemical improvement with resolution of fatigue. Zongertinib was resumed on February 11 and continued without recurrent hepatitis through June 2026.
CONCLUSIONS: The progression of liver injury despite zongertinib withdrawal, multiple prior immune-related adverse events, exclusion of competing causes, compatible histology, corticosteroid responsiveness, and absence of recurrence after zongertinib rechallenge collectively favored delayed immune-related hepatitis, although zongertinib-associated drug-induced liver injury could not be completely excluded. In similar cases, a structured etiological assessment, including liver biopsy when the result may alter cancer treatment, can help guide management.

title: Rare epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in completely resected stage I lung adenocarcinoma: a real-world study of mutation spectrum, clinicopathological features, and prognosis.
authors: Man L, Xia L, Li C et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rare epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations are heterogeneous, and their significance after complete resection of stage I lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. We evaluated the mutation spectrum, clinicopathological correlates, postoperative recurrence patterns, and survival outcomes of a study-defined primary rare EGFR mutation cohort after predefined exclusion of isolated T790M, exon 20 insertion-only disease, and major driver co-alterations.
METHODS: Consecutive patients who underwent R0 resection for pathological stage I LUAD with postoperative EGFR testing at West China Hospital between 2011 and 2024 were retrospectively identified. Rare mutation subtypes, compound mutation patterns, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and overall survival (OS) were assessed. Prognostic factors were evaluated using Cox regression, and outcomes were compared with classical EGFR mutations using 1:2 propensity score matching (PSM).
RESULTS: Among 1,357 EGFR-positive stage I LUADs, 176 patients formed the primary rare-mutation cohort. The most frequent rare mutation groups were G719X (n=104), L861Q (n=71), and S768I (n=24), with distinct compound mutation patterns. Five-year OS and RFS were 95.8% and 93.5%, respectively. A micropapillary component was associated with shorter RFS in the primary multivariable model [hazard ratio (HR) =4.062, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.134-14.544; P=0.03]. The unweighted number of pathological high-risk features was associated with RFS (global log-rank P=0.039), whereas adjuvant systemic therapy among stage IB patients and compound rare mutation status were not significantly associated with RFS. After PSM under comparable observed postoperative management, the rare-mutation group had similar OS and a lower recurrence risk than the classical-mutation group.
CONCLUSIONS: After exclusion of isolated T790M and exon 20 insertion-only disease, completely resected stage I LUAD with rare EGFR mutations showed favorable long-term outcomes. Compared with classical mutations, rare mutations were associated with lower recurrence risk and similar OS after treatment-balanced matching. Pathological features, particularly a micropapillary component, may help identify patients at higher risk of recurrence.

title: Real-world treatment patterns in stage IB-IIIC non-small cell lung cancer in China: the KEY-RAISE study.
authors: Zhong H, Yan S, Zeng J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths in China. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common type of lung cancer. The treatment landscape for early and locally advanced NSCLC changed considerably between 2019 and 2021. However, there are currently limited data available to inform optimal timing, sequencing, and combinations of different treatment modalities for early-stage NSCLC in China. Therefore, we conducted a real-world study of patients with stage IB-IIIC NSCLC in China to characterize treatment patterns and identify practice gaps.
METHODS: This retrospective, observational study was conducted at 10 sites across China in adults with newly diagnosed stage IB-IIIC NSCLC between January 01, 2019, and December 31, 2021 (identification period). The observation period was from treatment initiation to June 30, 2023. The primary outcomes included descriptions of treatment patterns by initial treatment modalities.
RESULTS: Patients (n=1,000) were mostly male (69.6%) with a mean age of 60.4 years, current/former smokers (52.9%), had non-squamous cell carcinoma (64.0%), and clinical stage III disease (54.8%). Among the 281 patients who received epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) testing, including 185 during surgery, EGFR mutations were identified in 174 cases (exon 21 L858R 47.7%; exon 19 deletion 33.3%). Of the 761 patients who underwent surgery (R0 resection 96.2%; lobectomy 83.6%), most received surgery plus systemic therapy (74.0%), primarily adjuvant treatment (79.6%). The rate of non-surgical treatments increased with initial clinical stage. Of the 239 patients not undergoing surgery, 78.2% received systemic therapy alone and 21.8% radiotherapy plus systemic therapy [concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT): 25.5%; sequential chemoradiotherapy (sCRT): 74.5%; immunotherapy consolidation: 26.9%]. Among the 600 patients who underwent surgery plus systemic therapy, 9.7% received neoadjuvant only, 79.7% adjuvant only, and 10.6% perioperative treatment, and the median real-world time on treatment (rwToT) was 2.1, 8.5, and 10.1 months, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides a reference for real-world treatment patterns for stage IB-IIIC NSCLC during the early immunotherapy period of treatment landscape change in China.

title: Antibody-drug conjugates in the perioperative treatment of resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a narrative review of research advances and prospects.
authors: Xiong Y, Sun L, Peng Y
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Even after perioperative chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy, pathological complete response (pCR) rates remain below 30%, and further improvement in long-term outcomes has stalled. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), leveraging targeted cytotoxicity and the bystander effect, can achieve tumor downstaging, micrometastasis clearance, and organ preservation in the perioperative setting, offering a new option beyond conventional chemoimmunotherapy. In this review, we aimed to summarize contemporary clinical evidence for perioperative ADCs in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and to provide practical guidance on patient selection, toxicity management, and future research.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov, together with the abstract books of major oncology congresses [American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO), World Conference on Lung Cancer (WCLC), European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO)], from January 1, 2018 to September 14, 2026 for English-language publications on ADCs in the perioperative treatment of resectable NSCLC. We included clinical trials, case reports, conference abstracts, guidelines, and authoritative reviews. Two authors independently screened and selected the literature; disagreements were resolved by consensus. Landmark studies published before 2018 were captured by reference-list screening.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: We cover TROP2-targeted agents (datopotamab deruxtecan, sacituzumab govitecan), HER2-directed trastuzumab deruxtecan, and bispecific EGFR-HER3 ADCs across neoadjuvant, adjuvant, and perioperative strategies, with attention to practice-changing platform trials such as NeoCOAST-2. Studies are grouped by therapeutic partner, namely ADCs combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors, ADCs combined with targeted agents, and ADCs administered as single agents in molecularly selected populations. We further examine how ADCs may substitute for, or complement, platinum-based chemotherapy, and how they interface with immune checkpoint inhibitors across the perioperative continuum. We discuss biomarker-guided patient selection, including TROP2 and HER2 expression and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based minimal residual disease (MRD); practical perioperative toxicity management (interstitial lung disease, oral mucositis, ocular and hematologic toxicity); and emerging mechanisms of ADC resistance. We also highlight future priorities, including MRD-directed, individualized adjuvant therapy and strategies to overcome resistance, to optimize ADC-based regimens for patients with suboptimal responses to standard treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: ADCs should be positioned as a complement rather than a replacement for perioperative chemoimmunotherapy.

title: Perioperative treatment for resectable non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations: a narrative review from advanced-stage evidence to whole-course precision management.
authors: Li Z, Han Y, Zhong W et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Epidermal growth factor receptor exon 20 insertion mutations (EGFR ex20ins) define a rare, structurally heterogeneous subtype of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that is relatively insensitive to conventional EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors. Although amivantamab, sunvozertinib, zipalertinib, furmonertinib, and other EGFR ex20ins-directed agents have expanded treatment options in advanced disease, their role in resectable NSCLC remains undefined. This narrative review summarizes the biological and clinical characteristics of EGFR ex20ins and critically evaluates advanced-stage evidence and emerging perioperative strategies.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, major preprint servers, oncology conference proceedings, trial registries, and regulatory sources were searched initially on June 3, 2026, with a targeted update on August 24, 2026. Peer-reviewed primary studies were prioritized; regulatory records, trial registries, conference abstracts, and preprints were included when they provided relevant emerging evidence. English- and Chinese-language publications were considered.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: EGFR ex20ins comprise heterogeneous insertion, duplication, and deletion-insertion variants with distinct conformational effects and drug sensitivity. Advanced-stage studies have established clinically relevant activity for EGFR/c-MET bispecific antibodies and novel EGFR ex20ins-directed tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), including randomized phase III progression-free survival (PFS) benefits for selected regimens. Perioperative studies are evaluating sunvozertinib, zipalertinib, furmonertinib, and amivantamab; however, evidence remains limited to ongoing trials, case reports, small series, and immature conference data, without mature randomized event-free survival (EFS), disease-free survival (DFS), or overall survival (OS) results.
CONCLUSIONS: Advanced-stage evidence supports perioperative investigation but cannot establish benefit in resectable disease. Progress requires accurate variant-level testing and randomized trials defining pathological response, surgical feasibility, toxicity, central nervous system (CNS) control, DFS, and OS.

title: Real-world outcomes of neoadjuvant targeted therapy in resectable epidermal growth factor receptor mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer: a retrospective study.
authors: Li J, Zhang Y, Gao J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Multiple clinical trials have validated the efficacy of neoadjuvant targeted therapy (NTT) for resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations. This retrospective study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) in real-world cohorts, and to compare therapeutic outcomes across different generations of EGFR-TKIs in patients with EGFR-mutant resectable NSCLC.
METHODS: Patients diagnosed with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma who received NTT between July 2018 and April 2023 were retrospectively enrolled. All participants completed at least two cycles of neoadjuvant EGFR-TKI therapy before surgical resection.
RESULTS: Forty-five patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma were enrolled in the study, including 18 treated with first/second-generation EGFR-TKIs and 27 treated with third-generation EGFR-TKIs. The overall objective response rate (ORR) was 57.7%, and the major pathological response (MPR) rate was 26.7%. No significant intergroup difference was observed in MPR rates. Rash, dry skin, diarrhea and oral ulcerations were the most frequent adverse events (AEs), and no statistically significant intergroup disparity was detected in AE incidence. No patient experienced grade ≥3 severe AEs. Subgroup analysis showed no significant differences in 1-year and 3-year relapse-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) between patients receiving first/second-generation EGFR-TKIs and those receiving third-generation EGFR-TKIs. Similarly, 1- and 3-year RFS and OS showed no statistical differences when stratified by early-stage versus locally advanced disease.
CONCLUSIONS: In real-world clinical practice, EGFR-TKIs used as NTT for patients with resectable EGFR-mutant NSCLC show encouraging therapeutic potential and are associated with an absence of severe adverse reactions. Patients receiving distinct generations of EGFR-TKIs as neoadjuvant treatment demonstrated comparable long-term prognostic outcomes.

title: Subtype-associated clinicopathological and tumor immune microenvironment heterogeneity in primary EGFR T790M compound-mutant lung adenocarcinoma: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Lin Y, Ye Z, Wu S et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) T790M-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is rare, and the clinicopathological characteristics and tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) of different compound-mutant subtypes remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to characterize the clinicopathological and TIME features of primary EGFR T790M compound-mutant LUAD and explore subtype-specific associations with disease-free survival.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 255 patients with surgically resected primary EGFR T790M compound-mutant LUAD. Tissue microarrays from 158 patients were evaluated using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). Disease-free survival (DFS) was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, while prognostic factors were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression for clinicopathological variables and Firth's penalized Cox regression for immune markers.
RESULTS: Primary EGFR T790M mutation predominantly occurred in compound-mutant form, with T790M+L858R being the most common subtype. Compared with T790M+L858R, T790M+19del had a larger maximum tumor diameter and higher frequencies of lymphovascular invasion, pleural invasion, and lymph node metastasis (all P<0.05). IHC and mIF analyses demonstrated subtype-associated TIME differences. The T790M+19del subtype showed an increased proportion of CD68+CD163+ macrophages and higher expression of immune-regulatory markers, whereas the T790M+L858R subtype showed relative enrichment of CD3+CD8+ T cells. In exploratory survival analyses, subtype-specific associations between TIME-related markers and DFS were observed: concurrent high expression of CD66b and CTLA4 was associated with shorter DFS in the T790M+19del subtype, whereas high TIGIT expression was associated with shorter DFS in the T790M+L858R subtype.
CONCLUSIONS: Primary EGFR T790M compound-mutant LUAD exhibits subtype-associated clinicopathological and TIME heterogeneity. These findings highlight the importance of considering accompanying EGFR activating mutation subtypes when evaluating this rare molecular subgroup.

title: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cfDNA liquid biopsy-guided neoadjuvant lazertinib in resectable EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a prospective phase II study.
authors: Kim IA, Kim H, Hur JY et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reliable preoperative molecular testing is increasingly important in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), particularly when tissue biopsy is not feasible or yields insufficient material. We evaluated the feasibility of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cell-free DNA liquid biopsy (BALiquid) as a preoperative epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) genotyping platform and assessed the clinical efficacy of neoadjuvant lazertinib in patients with potentially resectable EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
METHODS: A total of 128 patients with computed tomography (CT) findings suggestive of potentially resectable lung cancer underwent bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage near the target lesion. EGFR genotyping was performed using polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-based BALF cfDNA analysis. Patients with sensitizing EGFR mutations detected by BALiquid received neoadjuvant lazertinib for 9 weeks followed by surgical resection. Diagnostic performance, radiologic response, surgical outcomes, pathologic response, and safety were evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 48 patients with BALiquid-detected EGFR mutations, 40 were enrolled and 34 completed neoadjuvant lazertinib followed by surgery. BALiquid EGFR genotyping demonstrated a sensitivity of 74%, a specificity of 97.0%, a positive predictive value of 97.4%, a negative predictive value of 71.7% and 83.3% of concordance rate compared with surgical tissue genotyping. The all-treated objective response rate (ORR) was 57.5% [23/40; 95% confidence interval (CI): 40.9-73.0%], and the ORR in the per-protocol population was 67.6% (23/34; 95% CI: 49.5-82.6%). R0 resection was achieved in 33 of 34 patients. Pathologic downstaging occurred in 55.9% of patients, and major pathologic response was achieved in 6 of 34 patients (17.6%). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 4/40 patients (10.0%).
CONCLUSIONS: BALiquid may serve as a complemental preoperative EGFR genotyping approach to provide genetic information when tissue is unavailable or insufficient. BALiquid-guided neoadjuvant lazertinib demonstrated meaningful antitumor activity, favorable surgical outcomes, and an acceptable safety profile in patients with potentially resectable EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

title: Cannabis sativa phytoligands as potential EGFR inhibitors for lung cancer treatment.
authors: Owoloye A, Akinnusi PA, Olubode SO et al.
abstract: Lung cancer remains a major global health burden, and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) overexpression promotes tumour-cell proliferation, making EGFR an important therapeutic target. This study used an in-silico approach to evaluate Cannabis sativa compounds as inhibitors of the EGFR kinase domain. Among the compounds investigated, Luteolin-7 -O- glucoside, grossamide, and quercetin were the leading ATP-competitive inhibitors, with binding affinities of -10.878, -10.091, and - 10.000 kcal/mol, respectively. A four-feature pharmacophore model was generated from the lead compounds, which also showed favourable predicted pharmacokinetic profiles. During 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations (MDS), the EGFR-quercetin complex exhibited the lowest root mean square deviation of 0.9-1.5 Å, while fluctuation profiles revealed a relatively stable ligand-bound complex compared with the apo-EGFR. The MDS trajectory Molecular Mechanics/Generalized Born Surface Area analysis yielded binding free energies of -75.59 kcal/mol for grossamide, -56.90 kcal/mol for isovitexin, -49.11 kcal/mol for luteolin-7 -O- glucoside, and - 43.27 kcal/mol for quercetin, compared with - 47.41 kcal/mol for gefitinib. Electronic profiling revealed favourable orbital overlap and softness for quercetin and flavone glycosides within EGFR, while isovitexin showed superior kinetic stability and balanced solvation, supporting strong binding and active-site entry. These findings identify luteolin-7 -O- glucoside, grossamide, and quercetin as promising EGFR inhibitors and provide a baseline hypothesis for experimental validation.

title: Novel 4-Anilinopyrimidine-N-Acylhydrazone derivatives as dual EGFRWT/VEGFR-2 tyrosine kinase inhibitors against non-small cell lung Cancer: Design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and computational studies.
authors: Ibrahim TH, Kadry HH, Mohamed KO et al.
abstract: Two new series of 4-Anilinopyrimidine-N-acylhydrazone derivatives (7a-k and 9a-e) were designed and synthesized as potent dual EGFRWT/VEGFR-2 tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The in vitro antiproliferative activity of the compounds against MDA-MB-231, HepG2 and A549 cancer cell lines revealed derivatives 7e, 7i, 7k, 9a, and 9e were the most active, showing potent cytotoxicity against A549 NSCLC cells with IC50 values in the range of 1.25 to 7.20 μM compared to erlotinib (IC50 = 4.07 μM) and sorafenib (IC50 = 9.51 μM). Compound 9e was identified as the lead derivative with the most potent cytotoxicity against A549 cells (IC50 = 1.25 ± 0.11 μM), displaying 3.3- and 7.6-fold higher potency than erlotinib and sorafenib, respectively, with an excellent tumor selectivity over normal WI-38 fibroblasts (SI = 187.5). Enzyme inhibition assays confirmed potent dual kinase activity of 9e against EGFRWT (IC50 = 0.074 μM) and VEGFR-2 (IC50 = 0.055 μM) compared to erlotinib (EGFRWT IC50 = 0.043 μM) and sorafenib (VEGFR-2 IC50 = 0.098 μM). Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry revealed apoptosis as the primary form of cell death in A549 cells induced by 9e. Molecular docking into EGFRWT and VEGFR-2 revealed that 9e reproduces the critical binding contacts of both reference inhibitors and forms additional unique interactions, rationalizing its superior potency. The molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable complex formation of 9e with both targets, with favorable MM-GBSA binding free energies of -26.23 and - 38.97 kcal/mol for EGFRWT and VEGFR-2, respectively.

title: Empagliflozin Modulates Apoptosis and Autophagy Pathways in Lung Cancer Through Network Pharmacology and In Vitro Analysis.
authors: El-Feky OA, Hamouda SM, Tabaa MME et al.
abstract: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies. Empagliflozin (EMPA), a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, has demonstrated emerging anticancer activity; however, its effects on apoptosis-autophagy crosstalk in lung cancer remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the anticancer effects of EMPA and the influence of hydroxychloroquine (HCQ)-mediated autophagy inhibition in A549 and HOP-92 human lung cancer cells. Network pharmacology with explicit database association-score cutoffs, and molecular docking validated by redocking of a co-crystallized reference ligand, were used to identify potential EMPA-associated targets and pathways. Cytotoxicity of EMPA, HCQ, and their combination was evaluated by MTT assay, followed by combination index and Bliss analyses. Cell-cycle distribution and apoptosis were assessed by flow cytometry. Expression of apoptosis- and autophagy-related markers was evaluated by RT-qPCR, cleaved caspase-3 analysis, and Western blotting. Network analysis identified 239 overlapping EMPA-lung cancer targets, of which 46 were retained after applying an Open Targets association-score cutoff of 0.30. Docking, validated by reproducing the erlotinib crystal pose in the EGFR kinase domain (heavy-atom RMSD 1.30 ± 0.02 Å), indicated that EMPA can be accommodated at surface sites of ANXA8 (-7.6 kcal/mol) and the p62/SQSTM1 ZZ domain (-7.0 kcal/mol) and within the ligand-binding pocket of PPARγ (-7.5 kcal/mol; PDB 8BF1, the PPARγ-PGC-1α coactivator complex). EMPA reduced cell viability in both cell lines, with greater sensitivity in A549 cells. Combining EMPA with HCQ markedly reduced IC50 values and demonstrated synergistic interactions at IC50. EMPA altered cell-cycle progression and increased apoptotic cell death, accompanied by enhanced BAX and CASP3 expression and cleaved caspase-3 activation. EMPA increased LC3-II without p62 accumulation, consistent with increased autophagic activity, whereas HCQ-containing treatments induced LC3-II and p62 accumulation and enhanced apoptotic signaling. EMPA exerts antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects in lung cancer cells while modulating autophagy. Inhibition of lysosomal autophagic degradation by HCQ enhances EMPA-mediated cytotoxicity and apoptosis, supporting further investigation of this combination as an anticancer strategy.

title: 18F-FDG PET/CT Habitat Radiomics for Predicting Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Mutation Status in Locally Advanced Non-small Cell Lung Cancer: A Multicenter Study.
authors: Lian H, Deng H, Zheng J et al.
abstract: IntroductionAccurate identification of epidermal growth factor receptor mutation status is essential for treatment planning in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer, but tissue testing may be limited by specimen availability and sampling. We developed and externally validated a fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography habitat radiomics model to estimate mutation probability as an adjunct to molecular testing.MethodsThis retrospective multicenter study included 313 patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer who underwent imaging and tissue-based mutation testing. Center A provided the training cohort (n = 142) and internal validation cohort (n = 61), and Center B provided the external validation cohort (n = 110). Separate Otsu thresholds were applied to positron emission tomography and computed tomography intensities within each segmented tumor. Voxel-wise intersection generated four mutually exclusive habitats. Habitat features were selected in the training cohort and evaluated with six classifiers. Additional analyses examined adenocarcinoma-restricted performance, alternative partitioning, segmentation reproducibility, calibration, decision-curve performance, and selection bias.ResultsThe training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts included 69/73, 31/30, and 64/46 mutation-positive/mutation-negative tumors, respectively. The support vector machine habitat model achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.911 (95% confidence interval, 0.869-0.948), 0.898 (0.819-0.967), and 0.884 (0.829-0.933), respectively. With the threshold selected only in the training cohort, external validation sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and negative predictive value were 0.750, 0.739, 0.745, and 0.680. The combined model achieved an external validation area under the curve of 0.904 (0.855-0.949).ConclusionHabitat radiomics showed promising discrimination across two centers, including among patients with adenocarcinoma. The model may help prioritize confirmatory testing but should not replace biopsy, plasma testing, or molecular analysis. Prospective validation and direct biological correlation are required before clinical implementation.

title: ERBB2 Exon 20 Mutation-Guided Trastuzumab Deruxtecan Therapy in Metastatic Lung Adenocarcinoma with Low HER2 Expression: A Case Report.
authors: Gao ZF, Wen X, Yu JQ et al.
abstract: HER2 mutations are uncommon in lung adenocarcinoma, and treatment options become limited after failure of standard systemic therapies. We report a 69-year-old woman with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma involving multiple lymph nodes, bone, and the left adrenal gland. Histopathological and immunohistochemical examinations strongly supported a diagnosis of primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma. Targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) performed at initial diagnosis in January 2024 identified an ERBB2 exon 20 in-frame insertion mutation (p.Y772_A775dup). The patient received six sequential treatment regimens, including platinum-based chemotherapy, PD-1 inhibitor therapy, antiangiogenic therapy, and palliative radiotherapy. Initial tumor regression was observed, but sustained disease control was not achieved. Following further disease progression, the previously identified ERBB2 mutation was reassessed by the multidisciplinary team in 2025. HER2 immunohistochemistry showed an IHC score of 1+. Based on the activating ERBB2 mutation, trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) was initiated in June 2025 at a fixed dose of 200 mg per administration (approximately 3.2 mg/kg), lower than the standard starting dose for HER2-mutant NSCLC. Five doses were administered between June and November 2025. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 levels decreased markedly after treatment. Serial chest computed tomography indicated radiological disease stabilization for approximately 5 months, with no clinically significant treatment-related adverse events documented. This case highlights the value of molecular profiling in identifying actionable ERBB2 mutations despite low HER2 protein expression. It also provides a real-world observation of disease stabilization with a lower-than-standard initial dose of T-DXd, although conclusions regarding reduced-dose efficacy cannot be drawn from a single case.

title: Longitudinal TP53 dynamics in repeated tissue-based next-generation sequencing in non-small cell lung cancer: a real-world study with molecular lineage adjudication and sequential credibility verification.
authors: Zhao D, Xie D, Li K et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apparent TP53 gain or loss in repeated next-generation sequencing (NGS) may reflect technical noise, spatial heterogeneity, metachronous multiple primary tumors, or true clonal evolution. This study aimed to characterize TP53 longitudinal dynamics using a transparent verification framework.
METHODS: We analyzed 948 patients with non-small cell lung cancer undergoing at least two tissue-based NGS tests separated by ≥120 days (all specimens ≥20% tumor-cell content). Apparent TP53 flip events underwent two-step sequential verification: molecular lineage adjudication comparing complete variant spectra of sequential specimens, followed by an empirically anchored variant allele frequency (VAF) threshold (≥5%) derived from platform re-detection characteristics. Driver background and MET amplification were exploratory outcomes.
RESULTS: TP53 status remained stable in 824 patients (86.9%); 124 (13.1%) showed apparent gain (n=75) or loss (n=49). Lineage adjudication excluded 54 patients (5.4% of 1,002 eligible) with fully discordant driver spectra, whose apparent flip rate was three-fold higher than concordant patients (29.6% vs. 9.6%). Sequential verification identified 92 high-confidence events (64 acquisitions, 28 losses), showing no driver enrichment (EGFR 65.2% vs. 65.4% in the cohort; P>0.99). MET amplification did not differ across trajectories (high-confidence acquired vs. persistent negative: 8.9% vs. 6.3%; P=0.52).
CONCLUSIONS: TP53 alterations are largely stable during longitudinal monitoring. Many apparent flips reflect metachronous multiple primaries or near-detection-limit noise and are identifiable by a simple sequential framework. After artifact control, TP53 dynamics show no EGFR preference, and previously suggested MET associations were not confirmed under uniform ascertainment.

title: Alendronate-mineralized nanoparticles loaded with ALK-PROTAC reverse the resistance and rebound effects of ALK+ NSCLC to PROTAC therapy by disrupting the mitochondria-linked feedback.
authors: Zhang J, Yang L, Yan Z et al.
abstract: Targeted protein degradation technologies-particularly proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs)-have recently emerged as powerful tools in cancer therapy. However, it remains unclear whether tumor cells can mount immediate responses to proteolysis, potentially leading to acquired resistance and diminished therapeutic efficacy. This critical knowledge gap prompted us to investigate the underlying mechanisms and to develop preventive strategies. Here, we synthesized a PROTAC molecule targeting anaplastic lymphoma kinase-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer (ALK+ NSCLC), termed ALK-PROTAC (AP). We confirmed the presence of immediate adaptive resistance responses following AP withdrawal, characterized by rapid re-expression of ALK and accelerated cellular proliferation. Mechanistically, these adaptive responses were driven by a cascade of metabolic remodeling events, including enhanced glucose and purine metabolism, along with upregulation of genes associated with reactive oxygen species (ROS) and hypoxia responses. These processes were closely linked to mitochondrial function, thereby increasing energy production in ALK+ NSCLC cells after AP withdrawal, upregulating mitochondrial anti-apoptotic proteins, and enhancing the transcriptional activity of Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1). To overcome this resistance, we leveraged the metabolism-disrupting properties of bisphosphonates, specifically alendronate sodium (Aln), which induces mitochondrial dysfunction and metabolic perturbation via inhibition of the mevalonate pathway. We subsequently developed alendronate-calcium coordination nanoparticles encapsulating AP (Aln-AP NPs). As anticipated, Aln-AP NPs disrupted metabolic profiles, induced mitochondrial dysfunction, and abrogated AP-induced upregulation of anti-apoptotic proteins and YAP1. This intervention significantly delayed ALK re-expression and improved therapeutic outcomes both in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, these findings support metabolic intervention as an effective strategy to counteract immediate resistance to PROTAC-mediated proteolysis, addressing a key challenge in the field, expanding the scope of targeted protein degradation, and offering a novel approach to optimizing therapeutic efficacy.

title: Safety profiles of current and emerging neoadjuvant immune-modulatory and combination strategies in borderline resectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer: a narrative review.
authors: Berjaoui N, Siu YTR, Bille A et al.
abstract: Borderline resectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has no consensus definition. In an international multidisciplinary survey of stage III TNM subsets, no agreement on resectability was reached for 11 of 37 subsets, and the multisocietal consensus exercise conducted alongside it left the same anatomical configurations unresolved. This review adopts those non-consensus subsets as its working definition and asks how the safety profiles of current and emerging neoadjuvant immune-modulatory and combination strategies, spanning PD-1 and PD-L1 blockade, emerging checkpoint and immune-metabolic targets, antibody-drug conjugates and bispecific antibodies, bear on surgical decision-making within them. Six phase 3 trials now support neoadjuvant or perioperative PD-1 or PD-L1 blockade with platinum doublet chemotherapy in resectable disease, with pathological complete response rates of 17.2%-40.7% and event-free survival hazard ratios of 0.40-0.68. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events ranged from 32.5% to 73.0%, immune-mediated adverse events from 25.3% to 42.1% where an aggregate was reported, and treatment-related cancellation of surgery remained below 2% in every trial reporting it. Most patients who never reached resection did so for reasons other than toxicity. Among emerging targets, monospecific TIGIT blockade has failed in three randomised settings and the most advanced TIM-3 programme was discontinued on company-reported evidence, which recontextualises the earlier phase 2 signals for both classes. NKG2A, CD73 and TROP2-directed combinations have produced neoadjuvant pathological response signals without loss of surgical feasibility, although each rests on a single-arm platform cohort of fewer than 80 patients. One PD-1 and VEGF bispecific antibody has positive peer-reviewed phase 3 data in advanced disease and no neoadjuvant data. The operative question in borderline resectable disease is not whether response rates rise but whether toxicity, surgical delay and functional decline shift the risk-benefit balance in patients already marginal for resection. Answering it requires prospective cohorts in which borderline status is defined before treatment, of which MDT-BRIDGE and NEOINSPIRE are the first.

title: Salvage surgery for advanced non-small cell lung cancer after induction therapy with selective RET inhibitors: safety and feasibility.
authors: Deng HY, Li JH, Chen XL et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring rearranged during transfection (RET) gene fusions represents a rare molecular subset associated with an unfavorable prognosis. The advent of selective RET inhibitors has substantially reshaped the therapeutic landscape for RET fusion-positive NSCLC; nevertheless, acquired resistance remains an unmet clinical challenge, underscoring the need for alternative or combinatorial strategies. Here, we evaluate a novel therapeutic approach integrating salvage surgery with induction therapy using selective RET inhibitors.
METHODS: We retrospectively identified patients with advanced RET fusion-positive NSCLC who underwent salvage resection following induction therapy with selective RET inhibitors at West China Hospital, Sichuan University. Clinicopathological characteristics were systematically reviewed. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.
RESULTS: Between January 2022 and June 2025, 17 patients who received induction therapy with selective RET inhibitors followed by salvage surgery were enrolled. The mean age was 42.3 years, and 15 patients (88.2%) presented with advanced-stage disease. Induction therapy consisted of first- or second-line selective RET inhibitor treatment for a mean duration of 12 months (range, 3-34 months). All patients underwent salvage resection, with uneventful postoperative recovery and no major complications. No 30-day mortality was observed. Eight patients (47.1%) achieved a pathological complete response (pCR), while 13 patients (76.5%) achieved a major pathological response (MPR) including pCR. At a median follow-up of 26 months, the 3-year PFS and OS rates after salvage surgery were 75% and 100%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: Salvage surgery following selective RET inhibitor therapy was feasible in this highly selected cohort and was associated with favorable pathological responses and short-term outcomes. Comparative studies with longer follow-up are required to determine its oncological benefit.

title: SKP2-mediated CDK4 selective degradation contributes to SCP-7e-induced cell death of non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Yan Q, Ren H, Xu H et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: CDK4/6 are key cell-cycle regulators. CDK4/6 inhibitors encounter obstacles from therapeutic resistance and haematological toxicity, primarily due to potent CDK6 inhibition. Developing selective inhibitors against specific CDK members could address these limitations, but faces challenges from the high homology of ATP-binding sites.
METHODS: SCP-7 is a sesquiterpene lactone derivative with potent anti-non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) activity. Carbamate modification yields the optimised analogue SCP-7e. Biotinylated probe-based target fishing, MCODE analysis, DARTS, CETSA, SPR, circular dichroism and tryptophan fluorescence quenching analysis identified CDK4 as the target. The binding site on CDK4 was determined by LC-MS/MS, site-directed mutagenesis and covalent molecular docking. Co-immunoprecipitation was employed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms.
RESULTS: SCP-7 and SCP-7e selectively bind to CDK4, excluding CDK6 and promote the ubiquitin-proteasome degradation of CDK4. SCP-7e exhibits enhanced metabolic stability, superior in vivo anti-NSCLC activity, higher CDK4 binding affinity and greater degradation efficiency than SCP-7. Mechanistically, SCP-7e covalently binds to Cys78, a residue located outside the ATP-binding pocket of CDK4, thereby sterically blocking CDK4-cyclin D1 interaction and inducing SKP2-mediated degradation of CDK4.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identified Cys78 as a novel druggable site on CDK4 and provided a selective CDK4 degrader, advancing next-generation selective CDK inhibitors.

title: Validation of research site mentorship as an approach for increasing study site performance (enrollment).
authors: Johnson MR, Uddin AA, Johnson DK et al.
abstract: The identification of strategies that improve participant enrollment in clinical trials remains a key focus of stakeholders in this field, due to its role as a leading indicator of timely trial completion and its contributions to the validity and generalizability of clinical trial results. The VA Cooperative Studies Program (CSP) Network of Dedicated Enrollment Sites (NODES) replicated a previously piloted research site mentorship model in two actively enrolling CSP-funded clinical trials to validate its impact on study participant enrollment (CSP #2005: VA Lung Cancer Surgery vs. Stereotactic Radiotherapy trial (VALOR) and CSP #2008: Pentoxifylline in Diabetic Kidney Disease (VA PTXRx)). The "Total Randomized Participants (#) by Mentee Site" and the "Percentage of Randomized Participants (Actual/Expected) Monthly Average By Site (%)" were evaluated across participating mentee study sites over three time periods: 1) 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP), 2) 5-month intervention period (IP), and 3) 3-month follow-up period (FUP). These data were averaged across months during the respective time periods (PIP, IP, FUP). Our findings demonstrate an association between the NODES site mentorship model and improvements in most mentee sites' "Total Randomized Participants (#)" (4/7; 57%) at the end of the 5-month intervention period (IP), as compared to the 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP) (Table B). Increases in most sites' (5/7; 71%) "Percentage of Randomized Participants (Actual/Expected) Monthly (Average) By Site (%)" at the end of the 5-month intervention period (IP), as compared to the 5-month pre-intervention period (PIP) was also observed (Table C).

title: Efficacy and safety of stereotactic body radiotherapy combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors for non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis.
authors: Ji P, Zhao Z, Tang X et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) may augment antitumor immunity when combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but clinical studies span markedly different disease stages and treatment intents and have produced inconsistent comparative results. We aimed to synthesize the evidence and evaluate efficacy and safety, separating pairwise outcomes from descriptive single-arm outcomes.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through August 2026. Pairwise outcomes were synthesized as risk ratios (RRs) or reconstructed survival hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence interval (CI). Single-arm outcomes of SBRT plus ICI were summarized as pooled proportions. Published Kaplan-Meier curves were digitized and reconstructed as individual patient data (IPD). Disease-stage and treatment-setting analyses were prespecified as descriptive because they were based on unadjusted between-study comparisons.
RESULTS: Twenty-one studies enrolling 1,096 participants were included. Five comparative studies contributed to at least one pairwise outcome. SBRT plus ICI was not associated with statistically significant improvements in overall survival (OS) (HR 0.81, 95% CI: 0.52-1.25), progression-free survival (PFS) (HR 0.76, 95% CI: 0.53-1.10), or objective response rate (ORR) (RR 1.72, 95% CI: 0.85-3.51). Disease control rate (DCR) favored SBRT plus ICI (RR 1.20, 95% CI: 1.03-1.39), but significance was lost when either of two influential studies was omitted. Pairwise risks of any-grade and grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) did not differ significantly. In descriptive single-arm analyses, median OS was 36.4 months (95% CI: 29.8-50.9) and median PFS was 14.6 months (95% CI: 11.6-17.2); pooled ORR was 49.4% (95% CI: 38.0-60.8%), DCR was 80.6% (95% CI: 70.9-87.7%), any-grade AE incidence was 74.2% (95% CI: 50.3-89.1%), and grade ≥3 AE incidence was 27.1% (95% CI: 17.1-40.2%).
CONCLUSIONS: The comparative pairwise meta-analysis does not demonstrate an OS, PFS, or ORR benefit from adding SBRT to ICI-based treatment. Although the primary DCR estimate was statistically significant, its sensitivity to individual studies and the low certainty of evidence preclude a firm efficacy conclusion. Setting-specific randomized trials with standardized radiation, outcome, and toxicity definitions are needed.

title: A cross-sectional benchmark of seven large language models for National Comprehensive Cancer Network guideline adherence in non-small cell lung cancer management.
authors: Sun Z, Guan T, Geng J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While large language models (LLMs) show promise in general medicine, existing benchmarks lack the disease-specific rigor needed to assess guideline adherence. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) care requires alignment with rapidly evolving National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines. We developed an NCCN-grounded benchmark to assess guideline concordance of seven selected LLMs in NSCLC management.
METHODS: We developed an NCCN (Version 4.2025)-grounded NSCLC benchmark. The final analysis set contained 793 archived question-and-answer (Q&A) items. Each item included weighted positive criteria and safety-critical negative criteria. Seven specified LLMs were evaluated once per item, without a system prompt, retrieval augmentation, tools, or internet access. Automated rubric-based scores were used for descriptive comparison.
RESULTS: Across seven specified LLMs on 793 NCCN Guidelines-based queries, Gemini-3-Pro achieved the highest clean normalized score (0.739), while DeepSeek-V3.2 was the highest-scoring open-source model (0.695). Scores were generally higher for foundational tasks and lower for clinical-trial interpretation and therapeutic modality selection, with interpretation of clinical trial results showing the lowest task-level performance. Gemini-3-Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2 had the lowest omission rates (28.36% and 33.24%, respectively). Gemini-3-Pro had a 0% inclusion rate of rubric-defined contraindicated negative points in this benchmark. Automated scores are benchmark-specific and do not establish clinical safety or independently validated clinical quality.
CONCLUSIONS: This NCCN-grounded benchmark compares seven specified LLMs using a fixed question set. Although leading models performed better on several foundational tasks, the results reflect guideline-rubric concordance rather than clinical correctness and do not show readiness for independent clinical decision-making.

title: Development and impact of a quality improvement intervention to increase lung cancer screening in rural Appalachia.
authors: Gieske M, Avery D, Bittner-Fagan H et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer death in the United States, with rural Appalachian communities experiencing disproportionately high incidence and mortality rates. Limited access to low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening, socioeconomic barriers, and cultural factors contribute to delayed diagnoses and poor survival outcomes. The Association of Cancer Care Centers (ACCC)'s Rural Appalachian Lung Cancer Screening Initiative (RALCSI) aimed to reduce these disparities by strengthening the implementation of guideline-concordant lung cancer screening programs through workflow redesign, provider and patient education, and community engagement. The aim of this study was to describe the development and early impact of the RALCSI quality improvement intervention on lung cancer screening in rural Appalachia.
METHODS: From October 2023 through June 2025, a 10-county focus area in rural Appalachia was selected using epidemiologic data and Rural-Urban Commuting Area (RUCA) classification. A multiple-methods quality improvement (QI) approach was used. Baseline data were collected on site characteristics, screening volumes, and diagnostic yield. Interventions included provider training guided by task force members' expertise and ACCC's Lung Cancer Screening Implementation Change Package, targeted patient outreach adapted for the rural Appalachian context, and process improvements such as electronic health record (EHR) prompts and centralized scheduling. Quantitative metrics (first-time scans, repeat scans, interval scans, and lung cancer diagnoses) were tracked, while qualitative data from provider and patient feedback were analyzed to identify barriers and facilitators.
RESULTS: Two participating sites, Pikeville Medical Center (PMC) and Buchanan General Hospital in partnership with the University of Virginia (BGH/UVA), implemented new workflows and education programs to strengthen lung cancer screening. Screening volumes increased over the intervention period, with PMC performing 458 first-time scans and 543 repeat scans-an increase of 83% and 72%, respectively, compared to the 2023 baseline of 250 first-time and 315 repeat scans. PMC diagnosed 10 lung cancers through screening during this period. BGH/UVA conducted 75 first-time scans and 57 repeat scans, representing increases of 108% and 104% compared to the 2023 baseline of 36 first-time and 28 repeat scans, although no lung cancers were diagnosed during the study period. Providers demonstrated increased confidence in applying screening guidelines and engaging patients in shared decision-making, while patient outreach through trusted community channels improved participation. Persistent barriers included transportation challenges, follow-up adherence, accurate identification of eligible individuals for screening, and appropriate coding and billing of lung cancer screening services.
CONCLUSIONS: Community-informed, systems-based interventions can significantly improve lung cancer screening in rural regions. The ACCC RALCSI model demonstrates the value of combining provider education, culturally sensitive outreach, and workflow redesign to increase early detection and reduce disparities. Future efforts should focus on sustainability, policy-level interventions, and evaluation of long-term outcomes to support equitable access to screening nationwide.

title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptome analyses unveil that MYH11 links stemness to immunotherapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Xie Y, Xue Y, Lai D et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immunotherapy is an essential treatment strategy for lung cancer, yet resistance to it is often unavoidable, resulting in treatment failure and poor prognosis. The cancer stem cell (CSC) theory offers a valuable perspective for understanding tumor metastasis and resistance to immunotherapy. However, there is a scarcity of multi-omics studies that identify tumor stemness subpopulations and their associated signaling pathways. In this study, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with spatial transcriptomics sequencing (ST-seq) to identify a myosin heavy chain 11 (MYH11)-high stemness subpopulation linked to immunotherapy resistance.
METHODS: We conducted quality control and removed batch effects from two scRNA-seq datasets, then annotated cell types using established marker genes. Malignant cells were distinguished from epithelial cells with fastCNV. Stemness subpopulations were identified using a machine learning-derived messenger RNA (mRNA) stemness index (mRNAsi) and CytoTRACE analysis. To functionally characterize the stemness subpopulation, we employed Monocle3 pseudotime trajectory analysis, CellChat cell-cell communication analysis, and predicted transcription factors (TFs). We also performed consensus clustering on bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data, followed by immune-related scoring, immune cell deconvolution, and drug sensitivity prediction. Clinical validation was achieved through multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Experimental validation included short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-mediated MYH11 knockdown, real-time quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) and western blot analyses, and tumor sphere formation assays to assess cancer stemness.
RESULTS: We identified nine major cell types and found a significant enrichment of epithelial cells in tumors resistant to immunotherapy. Using fastCNV, we identified malignant cells and defined seven malignant cell subtypes based on stemness scoring. Notably, the Stem-subtype was significantly enriched in resistant tumors. Functional analysis showed that the Stem-subtype could differentiate into other malignant cell subtypes, with a strong enrichment in the NOTCH signaling pathway. Analysis of fibroblast subpopulations revealed that MYH11 + fibroblasts were closely linked to the Stem-subtype, collectively contributing to immunotherapy resistance. Consensus clustering identified two stemness-related subtypes, with Stemness I associated with poor prognosis. Immune scoring and immune cell analysis further indicated an unfavorable response to immunotherapy in Stemness I. Drug sensitivity prediction identified potential therapeutic agents, and in silico knockout experiments revealed downstream target genes. Validation with clinical samples confirmed that MYH11-high cancer cells were closely correlated with exhausted CD8+ T cell infiltration and poor immunotherapy outcomes. Experimental validation demonstrated that MYH11 knockdown significantly reduced the expression levels of CXCL12 and TUBA1A, as well as the expression of core NOTCH pathway genes. Furthermore, the tumor sphere-forming capacity was markedly suppressed.
CONCLUSIONS: In summary, our multi-omics analysis revealed a MYH11-high malignant cell stemness subpopulation and a MYH11 + fibroblast subpopulation, both of which are closely linked to immunotherapy resistance and poor prognosis in lung cancer.

title: Integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics for deciphering prognostic value and immunotherapeutic features of floatptosis-mediated cell death in lung adenocarcinoma.
authors: Wang H, Shi Y, Xue Q et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent research has uncovered an unprecedented cell death pathway induced by outer membrane vesicles derived from Bergeyella cardium variant (BCV). This process promotes the pathological fusion of lysosome-related organelles via the SLC9A9 protein, leading to the formation of large vacuoles and ultimately inducing a terminal vacuolar cell death termed floatptosis. However, the role of floatptosis-related genes (FRGs) in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains largely unexplored. In this study, we constructed a LUAD prognostic model based on FRGs to predict patient prognosis and further explored the characteristics of lysosome fusion-associated terminal vacuolar cell death (floatptosis) at the single-cell level.
METHODS: In this research, we systematically analyzed data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) databases to explore SLC9A9, an FRG. A total of 50 genes were screened out via co-expression analysis. The AddModuleScore algorithm was utilized to calculate floatptosis scores across different cell clusters, which were then divided into high- and low-score subgroups. The differentially expressed genes (DEGs) derived from the two subgroups were enrolled in weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to screen key gene modules closely linked to LUAD. Single-cell and bulk transcriptome analyses combined with WGCNA identified 74 FRGs. Genes contained in these modules were further analyzed by differential expression analysis and univariate Cox regression. Based on FRGs, consensus clustering was applied to identify molecular subtypes, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was utilized to establish a prognostic signature. Combined with multiple immune infiltration algorithms, tumor mutational burden (TMB) analysis and cell communication analysis, we explored the correlation between floatptosis and the tumor microenvironment (TME), so as to provide novel therapeutic strategies for LUAD.
RESULTS: A total of 74 FRGs were identified through single-cell and bulk transcriptome analyses, among which 11 exhibited differential expression between tumor and normal tissues. Of these, 7 genes were found to be significantly correlated with overall survival (OS). Pseudotime trajectory analysis of macrophages revealed that risk-associated genes were predominantly upregulated at later stages, whereas protective genes tended to decrease over time. Five of these genes were ultimately selected to establish a prognostic signature based on FRGs. Patients stratified into the low-FRGs group showed a markedly better prognosis than those in the high-FRGs group. Intercellular communication analysis further demonstrated that macrophages with elevated FRGs expression displayed enhanced activity in the C-C motif chemokine ligand (CCL), activated leukocyte cell adhesion molecule (ALCAM), and colony-stimulating factor (CSF) signaling pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: The prognostic model constructed based on FRGs allows for reliable survival prediction in LUAD patients and offers valuable insights into the immune microenvironment of LUAD. Notably, macrophages with high floatptosis scores can enhance the invasive and migratory capacities of tumor cells, making them promising novel therapeutic targets for LUAD.

title: Radiographic progression despite microbiologic clearance in pulmonary Mycobacterium avium complex disease revealing concurrent lung adenocarcinomaa.
authors: Kempanna K, Kunhi RM, Shah R et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) pulmonary disease and lung adenocarcinoma can present with overlapping clinical and radiographic features, creating a significant diagnostic challenge. Radiographic progression during treatment of pulmonary MAC disease is often attributed to inadequate microbiologic response or persistent infection; however, this assumption may delay recognition of a concurrent malignancy, particularly when microbiologic parameters otherwise suggest an adequate treatment response.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 78-year-old woman with bronchiectasis and previous microbiologic isolation of MAC was diagnosed with cavitary pulmonary MAC disease and initiated on guideline-directed multidrug therapy. Despite achieving sputum culture conversion, she developed new chest pain after approximately six months of treatment, and serial imaging demonstrated evolution of a previously cavitary right upper lobe lesion into a predominantly fluid-filled lesion with increasing surrounding consolidation. Bronchoscopy with biopsy revealed invasive pulmonary adenocarcinoma with coexisting necrotizing granulomatous inflammation. She subsequently underwent right upper lobectomy, with final pathology demonstrating a 6.5-cm poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, negative surgical margins, and no lymph node metastases (pT3N0).
CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that microbiologic culture conversion in pulmonary MAC disease should not preclude consideration of a concurrent malignant process when radiographic abnormalities continue to evolve. Discordance between microbiologic response and radiographic trajectory should prompt consideration of tissue diagnosis to exclude an underlying malignancy, potentially facilitating earlier diagnosis of lung cancer and preventing delays in definitive treatment.

title: Meditation Breathing Training and Short-Term Recovery in Patients Undergoing Thoracoscopic Lung Cancer Resection: A Non-Randomized Historical-Control Study.
authors: Huang X, Luo H, Dai Z et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association of meditation breathing training with short-term physical and mental recovery in lung cancer patients after thoracoscopic lobectomy.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A non-randomized historical control study design was adopted. A total of 62 patients (31 per group) diagnosed with lung cancer and receiving thoracoscopic surgery at our hospital between January 2023 and June 2024 were enrolled. Patients were allocated by admission period: 31 patients admitted from January to September 2023 were set as the control group (routine care and standard breathing training); another 31 patients admitted from October 2023 to June 2024 were assigned to the experimental group (additional meditation breathing training, twice daily for 10 minutes, from postoperative day 2 to discharge). Randomization and blinding were not applied. The primary outcome was exercise capacity (6-minute walk test, 6MWT); secondary outcomes included dyspnea (Borg scale), pain (Visual Analogue Scale, VAS), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, HADS), training compliance, and postoperative recovery indicators.
RESULTS: Following the completion of the targeted intervention, the experimental group showed greater improvements in exercise capacity (adjusted mean difference: +51.64 m; 95% CI: 17.28 to 86.00), dyspnea (adjusted mean difference: -0.65; 95% CI: -1.11 to -0.19), pain (adjusted mean difference: -0.52; 95% CI: -1.00 to -0.04), and anxiety (adjusted mean difference: -1.37; 95% CI: -2.43 to -0.30), and higher training compliance (87.1% vs 64.5%; OR: 3.71; 95% CI: 1.04 to 13.25) compared with the control group; however, the between-group differences in the primary outcomes did not remain statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (adjusted P = 0.019, 0.034, 0.173, 0.064, and 1.000 for exercise capacity, dyspnea, pain, anxiety, and depression, respectively). No significant between-group differences were observed for depression scores, postoperative pulmonary complications, chest tube duration, or hospital stay.
CONCLUSION: In this non-randomized historical-control study, meditation breathing training was associated with improvements in selected short‑term outcomes including exercise capacity, dyspnea, and training compliance; suggestive reductions in pain and anxiety were also observed, though these did not retain statistical significance after Bonferroni correction. Confirmatory randomized controlled trials are required.

title: Association of triglyceride-glucose and triglyceride-glucose body mass indexes with risk and prognosis of lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Jian Z, Chen S, Tang L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship of triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and triglyceride-glucose body mass index (TyG-BMI) with the risk of lung cancer and survival of patients with lung cancer remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to clarify the association of TyG index and TyG-BMI with the risk of lung cancer and survival of lung cancer patients.
METHODS: Several databases were searched up to July 2, 2026. Odds ratios (ORs) and hazard ratios (HRs) were combined to assess the association of TyG index and TyG-BMI with risk and prognosis of lung cancer, respectively. Subgroup analyses based on study design, tumor type, treatment and combination of diabetes mellitus (DM) were performed.
RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included. Pooled analyses demonstrated that higher TyG index [OR =2.42, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.54-3.81, P<0.001] and TyG-BMI (OR =1.01, 95% CI: 1.01-1.02, P<0.001) were significantly related to increased risk of lung cancer. Subgroup analyses based on the study design and tumor type manifested similar results. However, subgroup analysis based on the combination of DM indicated that the significant association of TyG index and TyG-BMI with lung cancer risk was only observed among the population without DM. Besides, a higher TyG index was associated with poorer overall survival (OS) (HR =2.24, 95% CI: 1.49-3.37, P<0.001) and progression-free survival (PFS) (HR =3.09, 95% CI: 1.78-5.37, P<0.001). TyG-BMI was also related to OS (HR =1.86, 95% CI: 1.36-2.56, P<0.001) and PFS (HR =2.34, 95% CI: 1.20-4.56, P=0.01). Subgroup analyses stratified by treatment and tumor type indicated consistent findings, but association of TyG-BMI with OS was only observed in non-diabetic patients.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated TyG index and TyG-BMI are significantly associated with increased risk of lung cancer and poorer survival outcomes, particularly among non-diabetic individuals.

title: A matter of size: 20-Fr vs. 24-Fr chest drainage after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy for non-small cell lung cancer-a randomized trial.
authors: Longo F, Sarubbi A, Nibid L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chest drains are routinely used after pulmonary lobectomy to evacuate air and pleural fluid and promote lung re-expansion. However, the optimal chest tube caliber remains controversial, particularly in the context of minimally invasive surgery. Smaller-bore drains may reduce discomfort, whereas larger drains may provide more effective evacuation of air and fluid. The aim of this study was to compare 20-Fr and 24-Fr chest tubes after uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (uVATS) lobectomy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with particular focus on postoperative pain, pleural drainage-related outcomes, and recovery.
METHODS: This single-center prospective randomized study included 80 patients undergoing uVATS lobectomy for NSCLC, who were allocated 1:1 to receive either a 20-Fr or 24-Fr chest tube (n=40 per group). The primary outcome was postoperative pain at 24 hours, assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS). Secondary outcomes included NRS pain at 12 and 48 hours, prolonged air leak (PAL), chest tube duration, subcutaneous emphysema, analgesic requirements, respiratory physiokinesitherapy outcomes, and length of stay (LOS). Pneumothorax (PNX) and pleural effusion (PE) were evaluated as exploratory radiographic outcomes.
RESULTS: The 24-Fr group showed significantly lower rates of PNX on postoperative day (POD) 3 (27.5% vs. 60.0%, P=0.003) and PE on POD2 (50.0% vs. 77.5%, P=0.01). Conversely, patients with 24-Fr drains reported significantly higher NRS pain scores at 12 hours [4.0 (3.0-5.0) vs. 2.0 (2.0-4.0), P=0.001], 24 hours [5.0 (4.0-6.0) vs. 4.0 (3.0-5.0), P=0.002], and 48 hours [5.5 (4.8-6.2) vs. 4.5 (3.0-6.0), P=0.02]. No significant differences were observed in PAL (27.5% vs. 47.5%, P=0.07), chest tube duration, subcutaneous emphysema, analgesic requirements, or LOS.
CONCLUSIONS: After uVATS lobectomy, 24-Fr chest tubes were associated with better early radiographic pleural control but greater postoperative pain. These findings highlight a trade-off between drainage efficiency and patient comfort and support an individualized approach to chest tube selection.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07827885).

title: A phase II pilot evaluation of lurbinectedin in patients with advanced gastrointestinal malignancies with DNA repair mutations.
authors: Viniotis AF, Jameson GS, Wertheim BC et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over 17% of gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies involve deficient DNA damage repair (DDR) mechanisms that have poor outcomes on standard chemotherapy but are sensitive to targeted therapies like immune checkpoint inhibitors and poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors. Lurbinectedin is an alkylating agent that demonstrated a 35.2% overall response rate (ORR) as second-line therapy in small-cell lung cancer patients who progressed on platinum-based chemotherapies. The drug inhibits DDR, promoting apoptosis in tumor cells through double-stranded DNA breaks (DSBs). Since repair-deficient tumors cannot efficiently and adequately fix these DSBs, DNA damage accumulates and results in enhanced tumor killing. Therefore, lurbinectedin's mechanism makes it suitable for use in cancers with DDR mutations. Our study evaluated the efficacy of lurbinectedin monotherapy in patients with advanced GI malignancies who harbored DDR mutations.
METHODS: This was a prospective open-label, single-arm phase II study at a single institution. Participants were age ≥18 years, had Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status score ≤1, and locally advanced unresectable or metastatic GI cancer with ≥1 deleterious DDR mutation. Intravenous lurbinectedin was administered at 3.2 mg/m2 on day 1 every 3 weeks. Hematology and chemistry labs were obtained on days 1, 8, and 15 of cycles 1 and 2, and day 1 of every subsequent cycle. Tumor markers (CA 19-9 or carcinoembryonic antigen) were collected on day 1 of each cycle. Tumor assessment via imaging occurred at least every three cycles. The primary outcome was ORR according to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Secondary outcomes included duration of response, tumor marker normalization, progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety using the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (NCI-CTCAE) version 5.0.
RESULTS: Eight participants (7 pancreatic cancer, 1 rectal cancer) with at least two prior therapy lines were enrolled and had DDR mutations in ATM (25.0%), ARID1A (62.5%), BRCA1 (25.0%), CHEK2 (12.5%), and FANC (12.5%). Median age was 63.5 years, 62.5% were female, and 87.5% were white. The ORR at 12 weeks was 0%. Median (95% confidence interval) PFS and OS were 1.2 (0.7-2.8) and 2.4 (1.2-4.1) months, respectively. The most common related adverse events (AEs) were grade 1 and 2 anorexia (50.0%) and constipation (25.0%); and grade 2 nausea (37.5%), anemia (25.0%), and fatigue (25.0%). Two patients (25.0%) experienced grade 3 and 4 neutropenia (1 each).
CONCLUSIONS: In this trial of individuals with advanced GI malignancies with known DDR mutations, there was no clinical benefit of lurbinectedin, as all experienced progressive disease while on the agent (NCT05229588). Interpretation of the study is limited by the small sample size, only two types of GI cancers represented, early termination, and that most participants (62.5%) only completed one dose of the drug.

title: Patient selection and risk stratification for lung resection: a narrative review.
authors: Lauricella LL, Terra RM
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Anatomical lung resection remains the cornerstone of curative treatment for early-stage non-small cell lung cancer, and patient selection is a major determinant of postoperative outcome. For more than a decade, preoperative assessment relied on three guidelines-American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP) (2013), European Respiratory Society/European Society of Thoracic Surgeons (ERS/ESTS) (2009) and British Thoracic Society/Society for Cardiothoracic Surgery (BTS/SCTS) (2010)-sharing a sequential approach of cardiac assessment, pulmonary function testing and, in selected patients, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET).
