Since then, minimally invasive surgery became standard, randomised trials validated sublobar resection, and evidence accumulated for new predictors, particularly the minute ventilation-to-carbon dioxide output (VE/VCO2) slope, frailty and sarcopenia. This review synthesises current preoperative risk stratification in light of the 2025 ERS/ESTS guideline and the 2021 American Association for Thoracic Surgery (AATS) expert consensus.
METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE for English-language literature on preoperative risk stratification and patient selection for anatomical lung resection, supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists and prioritising guidelines, randomised trials, systematic reviews and multicentre cohort studies. All numerical data were verified against the original publications.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: The 2025 ERS/ESTS guideline introduces formal assessment of frailty and nutritional status, endorses prehabilitation, and repositions risk-prediction models as tools for benchmarking rather than individual selection. Its exercise-testing algorithm considers peak oxygen consumption and the VE/VCO₂ slope together in three risk categories (peak VO2 ≥15, 12-15 and <12 mL/kg/min; slope <35, 35-40 and >40). The graded recommendation itself is confined to the use of CPET and does not endorse any specific parameter or cut-off, identifying only a peak VO₂ below 12 mL/kg/min or a VE/VCO2 slope above 40 as suggestive of high surgical risk. The AATS consensus independently ranks frailty and functional status above chronological age. Together, these developments support a shift from a binary judgement of operability to a structured process that also determines how to operate, adapting the extent of resection and the surgical approach to the patient's physiological reserve.
CONCLUSIONS: Contemporary risk stratification integrates cardiopulmonary physiology, ventilatory efficiency, frailty and nutrition with the configuration of the operation itself. Threshold calibration in the minimally invasive era, the optimal VE/VCO2 slope threshold and standardised frailty measurement remain unresolved.

title: Spread through air spaces (STAS) in stage I lung adenocarcinoma under the new IASLC/WHO pathological grading system: research progress on prognostic value-narrative review.
authors: Pan G, Yang G, Wang W et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Despite complete surgical resection, stage I lung adenocarcinoma exhibits a postoperative recurrence rate of 15-27%, exposing the prognostic limitations of the current Tumor Node Metastasis (TNM) staging system. While the 2020 International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) three-tier grading system significantly improves risk stratification based on high-grade morphological components, it does not incorporate tumor spread through air spaces (STAS), a recognized independent adverse prognostic factor. This review aims to systematically examine the incremental prognostic value of STAS within the framework of the new IASLC grading system and explore its clinical implications.
METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted using the PubMed database to retrieve relevant English-language studies. The review synthesized evidence focusing on the distribution of STAS across histological subtypes, its dose-response relationship with high-grade components, its impact on surgical decision-making, and the critical diagnostic distinction between true STAS and ex vivo artifacts.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Current evidence reveals a significant dose-response relationship between STAS and high-grade patterns; notably, the presence of even 5% high-grade components substantially elevates the risk of STAS. Retrospective cohorts consistently demonstrate that STAS strongly predicts disease-free survival and is a critical risk factor for local recurrence following sublobar resection. Crucially, STAS-positive IASLC Grade 2 tumors exhibit recurrence risks overlapping with those of Grade 3, supporting an "upstaging hypothesis" that warrants prospective validation. Furthermore, the clinical translation of STAS remains constrained by the high false-negative rates of intraoperative frozen sections and the ongoing debate regarding artifactual floaters.
CONCLUSIONS: Integrating STAS status as a collaborative parameter with the IASLC grading system constitutes a conceptual synthesis rather than an established clinical framework for stage I lung adenocarcinoma without necessitating additional molecular testing. Because the current evidence is based predominantly on retrospective data, prospective randomized controlled trial (RCT) validation is required before this approach can be regarded as best clinical practice.

title: Systematic review of pulmonary and cardiovascular disease among asphalt pavers.
authors: Sandvik A, Bugge MD, Nordby KC et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asphalt pavers may be exposed to a wide range of potentially hazardous substances, and an annual decline in lung function among asphalt pavers has been reported. Studies reporting a modest increase in lung cancer mortality among asphalt workers have been thoroughly summarized and reviewed.
AIMS: The aim of this paper was to systematically review and meta-analyse mortality from non-malignant pulmonary diseases and cardiovascular disease (CVD) associated with asphalt paving (PROSPERO Nr CRD42022341463).
METHODS: A librarian conducted a literature search in February 2024. We included human studies, assessed risk of bias, conducted meta-analysis and assessed confidence in effect-estimates using GRADE. We included cohort studies reporting estimates on mortality from non-malignant pulmonary disease and CVD among asphalt pavers compared with referents.
RESULTS: We included 10 cohort studies (3714 to 248 087 participants). Asphalt paving was associated with standardized mortality ratio (SMR) from all causes of 0.94 (95% CI 0.81-1.07), SMR from non-malignant pulmonary disease was 1.19 (95% CI 0.95-1.42), whereas SMR from CVD was 0.88 (95% CI 0.75-1.02).
CONCLUSIONS: Our study gave no support to the hypothesis linking asphalt work to excess mortality from cardiovascular or non-malignant pulmonary disease. The studies were not adequately adjusted for confounders. Healthy worker bias may have affected the results. From the GRADE assessment we are uncertain (very low confidence) about the association between asphalt paving and mortality from cardiovascular or non-malignant pulmonary disease. New studies, especially on non-malignant pulmonary disease with better control of confounding factors are warranted.

title: Functional decline at progression after durvalumab in stage III non-small cell lung cancer: prognostic impact and treatment patterns in a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
authors: Lisik-Habib M, Smółka K, Stando R et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Disease progression after durvalumab consolidation is frequent in unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the prognostic relevance of functional and nutritional status at first progression is insufficiently characterized. We evaluated their associations with post-progression overall survival (OS) and receipt of subsequent systemic therapy.
METHODS: This five-center retrospective cohort study included patients with histologically confirmed unresectable stage III NSCLC who received definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cCRT) followed by durvalumab and developed first documented disease progression. Clinical data were extracted using standardized case report forms. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status at progression, longitudinal body weight change from chemotherapy initiation to the last durvalumab administration, and post-progression treatment were evaluated. OS was calculated from first progression. The multivariable Cox model used complete cases; no imputation was performed.
RESULTS: Sixty patients were included, and 34 deaths occurred. ECOG performance status at progression was available for 59 patients; ECOG ≥2 was observed in 26 (44.1%) and was associated with shorter median OS (8.3 vs. 21.2 months; P=0.01). In the complete-case multivariable model (n=59; 33 deaths), ECOG ≥2 [hazard ratio (HR) 2.34, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.12-4.89; P=0.02], body weight loss ≥3% (HR 2.37, 95% CI: 1.10-5.07; P=0.03), and progression within 6 months of durvalumab initiation (HR 2.16, 95% CI: 1.07-4.35; P=0.03) were associated with worse OS. Forty-seven patients (78.3%) received subsequent systemic therapy.
CONCLUSIONS: At first progression after cCRT and durvalumab, impaired performance status was associated with poor post-progression survival. An exploratory, cohort-derived 3% weight-loss threshold and early progression also identified higher-risk patients but require external validation. Systematic functional and nutritional reassessment at progression may support individualized treatment planning, multidisciplinary supportive care, and realistic discussion of prognosis.

title: Factors associated with postoperative sleep disturbance in patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Weng Y, Zhao Y, Wang B et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) is common in patients following surgery, resulting in severe cognitive and mood disturbances, and even increase mortality risk. This study aimed to identify factors associated with PSD in patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer.
METHODS: We retrospectively identified sixty-two patients who underwent thoracoscopic radical resection of lung cancer at Tangdu Hospital, a tertiary teaching hospital in Xi'an, China, from June 2023 through October 2024. PSD was defined as a Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) score <60 on postoperative day 2 (POD2). Preoperative sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Pain was measured using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at rest and during coughing on POD1 and POD2. intraoperative fluid volume, and POD2 cough-induced pain, selected a priori based on clinical relevance and prior evidence. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with PSD.
RESULTS: Of 62 patients (mean age 67.5 years; 45.2% female), 36 (58.1%) met the RCSQ-defined criteria for PSD on POD2. Three factors were independently associated with PSD: preoperative PSQI score [odds ratio (OR) =1.58, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.19-2.10, P=0.001], intraoperative fluid volume (OR =1.004 per mL, 95% CI: 1.001-1.007, P=0.02), and POD2 cough-induced pain (OR =2.23 per point, 95% CI: 1.36-3.66, P=0.001). The model demonstrated good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.10) and discrimination (Nagelkerke R2=0.652).
CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative sleep quality, intraoperative fluid volume, and POD2 cough-induced pain were independently associated with PSD in this cohort. These exploratory findings highlight the importance of closer assessment of potentially high-risk patients, but require validation in larger prospective studies before being translated into definitive preventive strategies.

title: Prognostic value of changes in skeletal muscle index on serial computed tomography scans for overall survival in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a single-center retrospective study.
authors: Zhou YY, Guan YR, Wen Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survival rates in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) vary substantially, and changes in host body composition may affect prognosis. Serial computed tomography (CT) can repeatedly quantify skeletal muscle index (SMI) at the L3 level, but its dynamic predictive value and clinically usable thresholds have not been systematically validated. This study systematically evaluates the predictive value of longitudinal SMI changes based on serial CT for overall survival (OS), validate early treatment thresholds, and test its incremental effect over clinical models and Response Evaluation Criteria In Solid Tumors (RECIST).
METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort was established, including 451 patients with stage IIIB-IV NSCLC who received systemic therapy from 2018 to 2023. L3 SMI was extracted at baseline and follow-up CT; segmentation consistency intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) ≥0.97. ΔSMI% was modeled as a time-dependent exposure (per 5% decrease) in multivariable Cox, and a 12-week landmark analysis was used to evaluate early ΔSMI% ≤-5%. Baseline missing data were handled with MICE (m=20). Combined with RECIST, we compared the C-index, Uno time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), and 12-month net reclassification improvement (NRI), and conducted decision curve analysis and 1,000 bootstrap calibration.
RESULTS: Each 5% decrease in ΔSMI% was independently associated with increased death risk [hazard ratio (HR) =1.16, P=0.001], and higher baseline SMI was associated with reduced risk (per 10 cm2/m2 HR =0.87, P=0.006); the association between ΔSMI% and death risk was approximately linear (overall P=0.001). At the 12-week landmark analysis, early ΔSMI% ≤-5% was associated with worse survival (log-rank P=0.003), with an adjusted HR =1.68 (P=0.001). The correlation between early ΔSMI% and RECIST was weak (r=-0.18, P=0.001). On top of clinical covariates, adding baseline SMI and time-dependent ΔSMI% increased the corrected C-index from 0.67 to 0.71; 12-month NRI =0.19; AUC at 6/12 months was 0.71/0.70. Decision curves showed higher net benefit than treat all/none within threshold ranges 0.23-0.47 and 0.34-0.58; calibration was good.
CONCLUSIONS: SMI dynamic metrics derived from serial CT constitute an independent and actionable prognostic signal in advanced NSCLC, enable early identification of high-risk patients within routine follow-up windows, and provide incremental gains in discrimination and net benefit over clinical models.

title: Lung Cancer Incidence and Mortality in a Nationwide 45-year Prospective Cohort of Persons with Opioid Use Disorder.
authors: Wang X, Esposito E, Goedert JJ et al.
abstract: Purpose To examine lung cancer (LC) incidence and mortality in persons with opioid use disorder (OUD) in a national prospective longitudinal cohort. Methods Participants (N = 9895) were recruited from US medication-assisted treatment clinics. LC cases and deaths were ascertained through state cancer registries and the National Death Index-Plus. Covariates came from questionnaires and medical records. We calculated standardized incidence ratios (SIRs) and mortality ratios (SMRs) based on general population statistics; survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. Results There were 245 LC cases (56.7% distant stage at diagnosis) and 186 LC deaths, double the expected rates (SIR, 2.03, 95% CI: 1.78-2.30; SMR, 2.19, 95% CI: 1.88-2.52). Risks were similar among non-Hispanic Whites (N = 3227) and non-Hispanic Blacks (N = 3943), higher than Hispanics. SIR and SMR showed a dose-response trend with increasing smoking frequency. Among tobacco smokers with < 20 pack-years, the increased risk was similar to other pack-year groups. Risks were higher with HIV (N = 2079, SIR = 3.31, 95% CI: 2.43-4.40), for both prevalent and incident HIV. Median LC-specific survival was 76 months, 26 months, and 5 months, with local, regional, and distant stage at diagnosis, respectively. LC was frequently diagnosed at late stage. Conclusion LC incidence and mortality rates were two-fold elevated. Elevated risks with < 20 pack-years of smoking suggest current LC screening criteria may be too stringent for this population. Integrating LC and tobacco-cessation efforts into drug treatment programs, targeting both providers and patients, may reduce LC morbidity and mortality. Further research with larger, diverse cohorts is needed to confirm these findings.

title: PD-L1 transmembrane domain substitution overcomes CAR-T exhaustion driven by tonic signaling.
authors: Zhang L, Xu X, Yu H et al.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has achieved limited success against solid tumors, in part because excessive tonic signaling drives premature T cell exhaustion, as exemplified by CSPG4 and GD2 CARs. Here, we demonstrate that replacing the dimeric CD28 transmembrane (TM) domain with the monomeric PD-L1 TM domain substantially mitigates tonic signaling. The PD-L1 TM displays a smaller tilt angle and lower hydrophobic thickness, enabling a better membrane fit that minimizes spontaneous CAR clustering. This structural feature reduces tonic signaling and exhaustion and confers superior proliferation and memory preservation, resulting in enhanced and sustained tumor killing in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, these benefits were associated with attenuated phosphorylation across the CD3ζ-ZAP70-PLC-γ1/MAPK/AKT/NF-κB axis, downregulation of exhaustion-associated genes, and upregulation of stemness- and memory-related programs. Collectively, our findings establish that the PD-L1 TM swap is a modular and broadly applicable strategy to suppress CAR tonic signaling and promote durable, memory-biased CAR-T responses against solid tumors.

title: Reprogramming CAR-T cell function through synthetic cytokine receptors suppresses metastatic progression of TNBC.
authors: Hanna EA, Amitrano A, Forjaz A et al.
abstract: Patient T cells modified with chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) have shown remarkable therapeutic success in previously incurable cancers. However, despite its success in hematological malignancies, CAR-T therapy has shown only modest efficacy in solid tumors. The medical field has focused on developing new molecular designs that enhance CAR-T persistence, prevent exhaustion in the tumor microenvironment (TME), and increase the specificity of the CAR-T cell to various tumor antigens. However, much less effort has been placed on enhancing CAR-T cells' invasion into and migration through the stromal matrix of the TME, where they can elicit tumor-directed cytotoxicity. Here, we engineered CAR-T cells with synthetic cytokine receptors targeting inflammatory cytokines produced by the cells themselves, which increase their speed through collagen I matrices. We show that this enhanced motility is driven by increased CAR-T cell translocation through confined microchannels via cellular deformation, together with elevated migratory speeds in proximity to neighboring cells, suggesting improved responsiveness to local cues. These migration-enhanced CAR-T cells significantly reduce both primary tumor size and distant organ metastasis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) mouse models compared to standard CAR-T cells. These results support molecular design strategies that exploit mechanisms to improve cellular therapies for metastatic solid tumors.

title: Small-molecule inhibitors and checkpoint inhibitors in KRAS G12C NSCLC: balancing efficacy and toxicity.
authors: Wagener EDA, Noordhof AL, van Geffen WH

title: Surgical conversion after anaplastic lymphoma kinase-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (ALK-TKIs) therapy in N3 stage ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer: a report of three cases.
authors: Xiao B, Guo H, Zhang J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (ALK-TKIs) can produce substantial and durable tumor regression in ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We report three cases of stage N3 ALK-positive NSCLC patients who successfully underwent surgical resection after ALK-TKIs therapy.
CASE DESCRIPTION: Case 1 was a 45-year-old female who had stable disease (SD) after three cycles of docetaxel plus cisplatin and then received crizotinib 250 mg twice daily for 150 days. Tumor diameter decreased by 81%, and she underwent lobectomy with mediastinal lymph-node dissection. The resected lung lesion and sampled nodes showed pathological complete response (pCR) (0/12 nodes). She did not receive postoperative ALK-TKI therapy and developed an isolated brain metastasis 12 months after surgery; treatment with crizotinib and Gamma Knife radiosurgery achieved subsequent disease control, and the reported overall survival (OS) was 83 months. Cases 2 and 3 were 57- and 51-year-old males, who received alectinib 600 mg twice daily for 225 and 135 days, respectively, and both achieved partial response. They underwent wedge resection and segmentectomy with mediastinal lymph-node dissection. Pathology showed non-major pathological response (non-MPR) with 0/5 involved nodes in Case 2 and pCR with 0/10 involved nodes in Case 3. Both continued postoperative alectinib and were alive without recurrence at the reported 64- and 38-month follow-up points, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: We report that, in selected patients with stage N3 ALK-positive NSCLC, surgical resection after induction therapy with ALK-TKIs is a feasible therapeutic strategy. Maintenance ALK-TKIs postoperatively may contribute to favorable long-term survival outcomes.

title: Genomic characteristics, survival, and prognostic analysis of advanced non-small cell lung cancer with KRAS mutations and brain metastases.
authors: Chen Y, Yu X, Bao M et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The brain is a common site of metastasis in lung cancer. However, data on the incidence of brain metastases (BM) and survival outcomes among patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring KRAS mutations, particularly those receiving tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), remain limited. This single-center retrospective study aimed to characterize the incidence of BM in patients with KRAS-mutant NSCLC and identify prognostic factors associated with survival.
METHODS: A total of 4,021 patients with advanced NSCLC hospitalized at Zhejiang Cancer Hospital between January 2017 and December 2024 were screened. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), defined as the interval from BM diagnosis to death or the last follow-up. Survival curves were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and compared using the log-rank test. Prognostic factors associated with OS were evaluated using univariable and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analyses.
RESULTS: Among 301 patients with KRAS-mutant NSCLC, 57 (18.9%) had BM at initial diagnosis, and 91 (30.2%) developed BM overall. The incidence of BM according to KRAS subtypes was 36.1% (39/108) for G12C, 26.3% (10/38) for G12D, 32.4% (12/37) for G12V, and 38.1% (8/21) for G12A; no statistically significant difference was observed among these subtypes. At the follow-up cutoff date of March 5, 2026, the median OS of all patients with KRAS-mutant NSCLC was 23.5 months [95% confidence interval (CI): 21.6-29.2 months]. Among patients with BM, the median OS was 18.6 months (95% CI: 15.9-23.9 months). No significant difference in OS was observed between patients with KRAS G12C and those with other KRAS subtypes (22.4 vs. 17.4 months, P=0.18). After BM diagnosis, 70 patients received immunotherapy and 19 received TKIs. TKI therapy was not associated with an OS benefit among patients with KRAS G12C mutations (22.4 vs. 23.9 months, P=0.71). Patients with TP53 co-mutations had significantly longer OS than those without TP53 co-mutations (31.9 vs. 16.3 months, P=0.03). Patients receiving immunotherapy also had significantly longer OS (22.3 vs. 10.9 months, P<0.001). In addition, brain stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) was associated with improved survival (23.9 vs. 13.7 months, P=0.02). Multivariate analysis identified age, immunotherapy, brain SRS, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) as independent predictors of OS (all P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: BM is associated with an unfavorable prognosis in patients with KRAS-mutant NSCLC. TP53 co-mutations and higher diagnosis-specific graded prognostic assessment (DS-GPA) scores were associated with improved OS. Immunotherapy and brain SRS were significantly associated with prolonged survival.

title: Metastatic Lung Cancer to Non-vascular Soft Tissue and Lumbar Spine Mimicking Postoperative Scar at L4-5 Non-union: A Case Report.
authors: Sayegh J, Michael B, Carlyon T et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Soft-tissue metastases from lung cancer are uncommon, and metastatic involvement of a previous spinal surgical site is exceedingly rare. Such lesions may closely resemble expected post-operative tissue changes, creating a substantial diagnostic challenge. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of metastatic lung adenocarcinoma involving a non-vascular superficial compartment at the site of a prior lumbar fusion non-union.
CASE REPORT: A 69-year-old man with a history of staged lumbar spine surgery presented for revision decompression and fusion. During the procedure, an approximately 2.5 × 5.1 cm mass superficial to the deep spinal fascia, initially suspected to represent post-surgical scarring, was identified. Frozen section revealed metastatic adenocarcinoma. Further workup identified a KRAS G12C-mutated lung adenocarcinoma with widespread metastases involving bone, lung, adrenal gland, and posterior lumbar soft tissues. Despite timely initiation of chemotherapy and radiotherapy after diagnosis, the patient died a few months later.
CONCLUSION: Soft-tissue metastases to prior spinal surgical sites are exceedingly rare and may mimic post-operative changes. Surgeons should maintain suspicion for malignancy when encountering atypical tissue during revision spine procedures, as accurate and timely diagnosis is essential for appropriate oncologic staging and treatment planning.

title: Final efficacy and safety data from the Phase I/II ARROW study of pralsetinib in patients with advanced REarranged during Transfection fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Roskoski R

title: Typical Carcinoid Tumor of the Lung: A Case Report Demonstrating Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Database Analysis.
authors: Kulkarni N, Albrecht R
abstract: Typical lung carcinoid tumors are classified as well-differentiated, low-grade (G1) neuroendocrine neoplasms. This case study details the clinical course, diagnostic complexity, and definitive management of a 41-year-old African American male diagnosed with a histologically confirmed typical carcinoid (G1) that manifested a highly aggressive anatomical phenotype. Key features included bulky multi-station ipsilateral mediastinal lymph node metastasis (N2 disease), prevalent lymphovascular invasion, and direct phrenic nerve involvement. Following definitive surgical resection (left upper lobe segmentectomy), the disease was pathologically staged as pT2a N2 M0 (Stage IIIA).

title: Age and the association of radiotherapy with survival in extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer: an exploratory secondary analysis of two observational cohorts.
authors: Zhang S, Liu Y, Zhou X et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thoracic radiotherapy is an option for some patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), but it is unclear how it should be used after first-line chemoimmunotherapy and whether its value differs with age. In two observational datasets that defined radiotherapy exposure differently, we asked whether age changed the association between radiotherapy and overall survival (OS).
METHODS: We studied a historical Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) cohort diagnosed in 2010-2015 and re-analyzed a previously published multicenter cohort of 171 patients given first-line chemoimmunotherapy in Sichuan. In SEER the exposure was recorded first-course radiotherapy, which is not the same as consolidative thoracic radiotherapy (cTRT). The primary SEER cohort contained 13,676 patients with distant metastasis, and one global propensity-score match (PSM) produced 4,116 pairs. In the institutional cohort we fitted a time-varying Cox model for cTRT and OS; 33 patients with 33 deaths had complete data for the adjusted model. Age was treated as continuous, and we tested treatment-by-age interactions in both cohorts.
RESULTS: In SEER, recorded first-course radiotherapy was associated with lower all-cause mortality in the multivariable model [hazard ratio (HR) 0.75, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.72-0.78; P<0.001]; the matched cohort gave a similar estimate (HR 0.72, 95% CI: 0.69-0.75; P<0.001). Age did not interact with radiotherapy (ratio of HRs per 10-year increase 1.02, 95% CI: 0.98-1.06; likelihood-ratio P=0.36). In the institutional time-varying Cox analysis, cTRT was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.40, 95% CI: 0.17-0.98; P=0.04), and here the interaction was apparent (ratio 0.27 per 10-year increase, 95% CI: 0.11-0.64; Wald P=0.003; likelihood-ratio P=0.01). At age 65 years, the model-derived cTRT HR was 0.35 (95% CI: 0.16-0.78; P=0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: In the SEER cohort, recorded first-course radiotherapy was associated with OS, and the interaction with age was not statistically significant. In the Sichuan cohort, the time-varying model gave an overall cTRT HR of 0.40 and a significant continuous age-by-cTRT interaction. That model, however, rested on 33 complete cases and on covariates chosen by outcome screening, two of which were measured after treatment began. These findings establish neither a validated age threshold nor a causal age-specific treatment effect.

title: POEM for paraneoplastic achalasia type II in a patient with anti-Hu antibody-positive small cell lung cancer.
authors: Samnani S, Alkhurassi H, Woodman K
abstract: Achalasia is an esophageal motility disorder marked by impaired lower esophageal sphincter relaxation and absent peristalsis. Rarely, it occurs as a paraneoplastic syndrome, especially with small cell lung cancer (SCLC) and anti-Hu antibodies. We report a 74-year-old woman with prior limited-stage SCLC who developed progressive dysphagia and weight loss. Workup showed anti-Hu positivity and type II achalasia on manometry, with stable lung nodules. Botulinum toxin and IVIG provided minimal benefit, but POEM led to significant symptom improvement and resolution of esophageal retention.

title: Radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors in small cell lung cancer: a Web of Science Core Collection-based bibliometric analysis.
authors: Wang W, Chen Z, Wang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy (RT) combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for small cell lung cancer (SCLC). However, the global research landscape, knowledge structure, and evolving trends in this field have not been systematically investigated. This study aimed to provide a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research on RT combined with ICIs for SCLC.
METHODS: The Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) was searched on 4 June 2026. Publications related to RT combined with ICIs for SCLC were identified according to predefined eligibility criteria. Bibliometric analyses were performed using VOSviewer (version 1.6.21) and CiteSpace (version 7.0.R0) to evaluate publication trends, collaborations among authors, institutions, and countries/regions, journal characteristics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation networks, keyword clustering, and emerging research hotspots.
RESULTS: Of 341 retrieved records, 112 publications met the eligibility criteria. Annual publication output increased markedly after 2022, peaked at 23 publications in 2023, and remained within a similar range in subsequent complete years. Publications identified in 2026 represented year-to-date data, with the annual output expected to remain within a comparable range based on the observed publication pattern. The 112 publications involved 1,014 authors, 692 institutions, 56 journals, and 63 countries/regions. China ranked first in publication output (61 publications) and citations [759], whereas the United States demonstrated extensive international collaboration. The Journal of Thoracic Oncology and Annals of Oncology published the largest number of articles, whereas the New England Journal of Medicine had the highest citation count. Landmark clinical trials formed the core knowledge base of the field. Keyword analyses indicated that recent research has shifted toward limited-stage disease, durvalumab-based strategies, chemoradiotherapy, multicenter studies, and other treatment optimization approaches.
CONCLUSIONS: Research on RT combined with ICIs for SCLC has expanded substantially since 2022 but has subsequently entered a relatively stable stage. Current research is driven by landmark clinical trials and increasingly focuses on optimizing multimodal treatment strategies. These findings provide a comprehensive overview of the field and may help to guide future research priorities and international collaboration.

title: Immunotherapy maintenance in extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer: a real-world retrospective study.
authors: Lin X, Lin N, Zhang Q et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are commonly continued as maintenance therapy after induction for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), survival remains poor and real-world evidence specifically evaluating post-induction maintenance immunotherapy is limited. This study aimed to evaluate the association between post-induction maintenance immunotherapy and survival outcomes in patients with ES-SCLC treated with first-line chemoimmunotherapy.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 263 patients with ES-SCLC who received first-line platinum-etoposide chemotherapy plus an ICI. Primary analyses were performed in a landmark cohort of patients alive and progression-free after induction chemoimmunotherapy to reduce immortal-time and guarantee-time bias. Landmark-defined overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were compared between maintenance and non-maintenance groups using Kaplan-Meier analysis and treatment-adjusted Cox models. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), propensity score matching (PSM), and an actual/pseudo-index date analysis were performed as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: The landmark cohort included 235 patients (128 maintenance, 107 non-maintenance). Maintenance immunotherapy was associated with longer landmark-defined OS (median, 370 vs. 243 days; P<0.01) and PFS (median, 209 vs. 124 days; P<0.01). In adjusted Cox models, maintenance remained associated with improved OS [hazard ratio (HR) =0.70; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.50-0.97] and PFS (HR =0.70; 95% CI: 0.52-0.92). IPTW analyses yielded similar estimates for OS (HR =0.71; 95% CI: 0.51-0.98) and PFS (HR =0.69; 95% CI: 0.52-0.91). PSM analyses were exploratory and showed attenuated, non-significant estimates. In the actual/pseudo-index analysis (174 patients), maintenance remained associated with OS (HR =0.49; 95% CI: 0.30-0.78), whereas the PFS estimate was attenuated and non-significant (HR =0.71; 95% CI: 0.47-1.05; P=0.089).
CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide hypothesis-generating real-world evidence supporting further prospective evaluation of maintenance immunotherapy as a post-induction strategy in selected patients with ES-SCLC.

title: First-line systemic treatment patterns and outcomes in lung cancer patients with malignant pleural effusion: a retrospective multicenter study.
authors: Zhang Y, Wang R, Xiang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a frequent complication of advanced lung cancer with poor prognosis. The optimal first-line systemic treatment for these patients remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate first-line systemic treatment patterns and outcomes in lung cancer patients with MPE.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study across 27 centers in China evaluated the efficacy and safety of first-line systemic therapy in lung cancer patients with MPE from 2013 to 2024. The primary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).
RESULTS: Of 1,029 patients included, 88.1% had non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and 11.9% had small cell lung cancer (SCLC); 87.4% received first-line systemic therapy. SCLC patients received chemotherapy alone (50.8%; 62/122) or combined with immunotherapy (47.5%; 58/122). Most driver gene-positive NSCLC patients received targeted therapy (91.4%; 415/454). Driver gene-negative NSCLC patients primarily received chemotherapy alone (27.8%; 126/453), chemotherapy plus immunotherapy (15.9%; 72/453), or chemotherapy plus bevacizumab (17.9%; 81/453). Median OS for the overall cohort was 26.1 months. Systemic therapy significantly extended median OS compared to no systemic therapy (28.1 vs. 12.7 months; P<0.001). Driver gene-positive NSCLC had longer OS than driver gene-negative patients (34.1 vs. 22.6 months; P<0.001). In SCLC, no significant PFS or OS difference was observed between the two regimens. After adjustment, targeted combination therapy versus monotherapy showed non-significant trends for PFS [hazard ratio (HR), 0.74; P=0.09] and OS (HR, 0.67; P=0.10) among driver gene-positive NSCLC. Among driver gene-negative NSCLC, chemotherapy plus bevacizumab significantly improved median OS versus chemotherapy alone (41.8 vs. 21.4 months; P=0.04) and was an independent predictor of favorable OS [HR, 0.59; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.38-0.90; P=0.02], despite no significant PFS improvement (HR, 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-1.01; P=0.055), with a manageable safety profile [grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs): 14.8%].
CONCLUSIONS: First-line systemic therapy was associated with improved survival in lung cancer patients with MPE, though outcomes differed according to histologic and molecular subtypes. The addition of bevacizumab to chemotherapy was independently associated with longer OS among patients with driver gene-negative NSCLC with MPE.

title: Clinical and prognostic characteristics of concurrent small cell lung cancer in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a retrospective study.
authors: Shi Y, Li Z, Chen R et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer (LC) is a comorbidity that seriously affects the prognosis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients. Small cell LC (SCLC) accounts for the highest proportion of hospitalized LC patients with concurrent IPF at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH). To enable effective and standardized management of patients with IPF and SCLC, this study aims to summarize the clinical and prognostic characteristics of IPF-SCLC patients to improve their prognosis.
METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled patients with IPF (diagnosed by 2022 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT criteria)-SCLC (pathologically confirmed) admitted to PUMCH from January 2014 to December 2023. Clinical manifestation, chest computed tomography (CT) imaging, laboratory test, treatment and outcome data of patients with IPF-SCLC were collected and reviewed in detail with final follow-up on June 30, 2024.
RESULTS: Forty patients with IPF-SCLC were included with the average age of 68.2±6.3 years (range, 54 to 82 years). And there were 37 (92.5%) males. Median follow-up time was 12.0 months. Additionally, 35 (87.5%) patients had a smoking history. Twenty-eight (70.0%) IPF-SCLC patients were concurrent with one or more other underlying diseases. Emphysema was detected in 26 (65%) patients via chest CT. IPF and SCLC were diagnosed during the same period in 23 (57.5%) patients, whereas SCLC was diagnosed during the follow-up of IPF in the remaining 17 patients. However, pirfenidone and nintedanib were only prescribed to two patients, respectively. Most patients were diagnosed with late-stage SCLC: 17 (42.5%) patients had stage IV SCLC, and 15 (37.5%) patients had stage III SCLC. Furthermore, with respect to anticancer therapy, one (2.5%) patient received no chemotherapy, 2 (5%) patients received oral etoposide, 37 (92.5%) patients received intravenous chemotherapy, and 11 (27.5%) patients received pulmonary radiotherapy. Finally, 29 (72.5%) patients died during follow-up. The main causes of death were acute exacerbation of IPF (AE-IPF) (13 patients, 44.8%) and progression of SCLC (12 patients, 41.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: The patients with IPF-SCLC included in our studies were mainly elderly males with a heavy smoking index, most of whom were diagnosed with late-stage SCLC. Antifibrotic medications for IPF were uncommon, and chemotherapy was the main cancer treatment. The progression of uncontrolled SCLC and AE-IPF were the main causes of death. Clinicians should consider early initiation of antifibrotic therapy alongside chemotherapy, monitor for the occurrence of AE-IPF, and adopt multidisciplinary management.

title: From risk factors to individualized prediction: development and internal validation of a machine learning model for early identification of postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery.
authors: Petrovic S, Gabršček T, Beovic B et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pneumonia (POP) remains one of the most common infectious complications following lung cancer surgery and is associated with substantial morbidity. Although several risk factors for POP have been identified, clinically applicable approaches for early individualized risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models for early prediction of POP using routinely available perioperative variables.
METHODS: In this prospective single-center cohort study, 258 consecutive patients undergoing pulmonary resection for non-small cell lung cancer or pulmonary carcinoid tumors were screened, of whom 200 were included in the final study cohort. POP was defined by newly developed postoperative radiographic abnormalities accompanied by clinical signs of infection requiring antibiotic therapy. Machine learning models, including logistic regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), random forest (RF), and XGBoost (XGB), were developed to predict POP using demographic, clinical, laboratory, surgical, and postoperative day 1 radiographic variables. Model performance was assessed using nested leave-one-out cross-validation and quantified by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). A nomogram was constructed from the best-performing model to facilitate individualized risk estimation. Different decision thresholds were explored to evaluate clinically relevant trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity.
RESULTS: POP occurred in 47 of 200 patients (23.5%), while no POP-related mortality was observed. LR demonstrated the best predictive performance (AUROC 0.701±0.070), followed by NB (0.698±0.103), RF (0.656±0.217), and XGB (0.589±0.179). The most influential predictors included advanced age, perioperative changes in C-reactive protein concentration (ΔCRP), elevated preoperative CRP levels, prolonged operative duration, and abnormal postoperative day 1 chest radiographic findings. At a decision threshold of 25%, the model correctly identified 25 of 47 POP cases (53.2%), whereas increasing the threshold to 32.5% reduced false-positive classifications from 42 to 24 at the expense of missing an additional four POP cases.
CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning models based on routinely available perioperative variables enabled early individualized prediction of POP following lung cancer surgery. LR provided the best balance between predictive performance, stability, and interpretability, allowing the development of an interpretable nomogram for individualized risk estimation. The model may have potential to support risk-adapted postoperative surveillance and more efficient allocation of healthcare resources; however, external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Prognostic prediction of pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma using a transformer-based artificial intelligence model: a two-center retrospective cohort study.
authors: Liu L, Liang L, Wang D et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinomas (pNECs) are a rare and heterogeneous group of malignancies, ranging from low-grade carcinoids to high-grade small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) and large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC). Prognostic tools for these tumors are scarce and have rarely been validated in external cohorts.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop a Transformer-based prognostic prediction model for pNEC and validate it in an independent external cohort, to improve survival estimation and support individualized treatment decisions.
METHODS: This retrospective two-center cohort study included 823 patients with surgically resected pNEC (2001-2023). Models were developed in Center 1 (n=374; randomly split 8:2 into training and internal test sets) and externally validated in an independent Center 2 cohort (n=449). Three algorithms-logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), and the Transformer-based tabular foundation model TabPFN-were compared for estimating overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) at 1-, 3-, and 5-year landmarks, with evaluation by receiver operating characteristic, calibration, and decision curve analyses, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis for interpretability.
RESULTS: TabPFN achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) in most tasks in both test sets, with task-dependent exceptions: in the internal test set, logistic regression performed best for 1-year OS (AUC 0.885), while TabPFN performed best for the remaining tasks, including 3-year OS (0.880), overall DFS (0.810), and 1-year DFS (0.892); in the external test set, TabPFN remained best for 1- and 3-year OS and for overall, 1-, and 3-year DFS (0.747-0.802), whereas logistic regression performed best for 5-year OS and DFS. External calibration was less satisfactory. Disease stage, pathological subtype, and age were the key prognostic predictors, and TabPFN was more accurate for low-grade subtypes. SHAP analysis quantified the contribution of each feature and made the model interpretable.
CONCLUSIONS: The Transformer-based model improves survival estimation in pNEC, with task-dependent advantages over conventional methods and confirmed transportability to an independent institutional cohort. Prospective multicenter validation and calibration refinement are needed before broader clinical use.

title: Clinical impact of traditional Chinese medicine in combination with chemotherapy in the therapy of extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.
authors: Qin W, Zhang D, Zhang L
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We investigated the clinical impact of traditional Chinese medicine in combination with chemotherapy in treating extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. Methods: One hundred and two patients admitted to our hospital from October 2022 to August 2023 were included. The control group received irinotecan hydrochloride for injection. On the basis of the control group, the study group was given Kangai injection.
RESULTS: The objective response rate and clinical benefit rate values of the study group presented higher than the control group, the decline of tumor markers was more obvious, the levels of CD4+ and CD4+/CD8+ were higher, the CD8+ level was lower. Incidence of adverse drug reactions in the study group (7.84%) presented reduction as relative to the control group (25.49%). After therapy, the elevation of quality of life score was more obvious in the study group as relative to the control group.
CONCLUSION: Traditional Chinese medicine in combination with chemotherapy can promote the short-term efficacy, reduce the levels of tumor markers, regulate the immune function of patients, lessen the occurrence of adverse reactions, along with help promote the quality of life of patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer.

title: Radiomics analysis of brain-tumor interface on multiparametric MRI for prediction of brain metastasis primary site.
authors: Jiang M, Han B, Huang Y et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Brain metastasis (BM) frequently occurs in advanced cancer patients, and accurate identification of the primary origin is essential for personalized treatment. Conventional imaging often lacks sensitivity and specificity for BM source prediction. This study aimed to develop and validate a multiparametric MRI-based radiomics model emphasizing brain-tumor interface (BTI) features to improve noninvasive BM origin identification.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: The primary cohort included 429 patients (740 BMs) from two centers, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), small cell lung cancer (SCLC), breast cancer (BC), and gastrointestinal cancer (GIC), and an independent validation cohort of 33 patients (84 BMs) from a third center. All underwent pre-treatment 3.0 T MRI with T1-weighted contrast-enhanced (T1CE) and T2-weighted (T2W) sequences. Radiomic features were extracted from tumor core and BTI regions (2, 4, 6, 8 mm). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection, and radiomics signatures (RS) were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis.
RESULTS: The constructed RS-BTI4 based on the 4-mm BTI region generated the best overall performance, with area under the ROC curve (AUCs) in the training cohort were 0.855 (LC/NLC), 0.910 (SCLC/NSCLC), and 0.890 (BC/GIC); in validation cohort, 0.726, 0.856, and 0.809; and in external validation cohort, 0.739, 0.750, and 0.792, respectively. RS-BTI4 consistently outperformed models based on other BTI radial widths and the whole tumor region in identifying the primary origin of BM.
CONCLUSION: BTI-derived radiomic features demonstrate strong potential for noninvasive identification of BM origin, with the 4-mm BTI region showing optimal predictive performance.
KEY POINTS: Question Conventional MRI cannot reliably identify the primary origin of brain metastases, particularly when the primary tumor remains unknown at diagnosis. Findings The 4-mm brain-tumor interface model showed the most favorable overall performance, measured by area under the curve, across three binary classification tasks and validation cohorts. Critical relevance statement Integrating brain-tumor interface radiomics with multiparametric MRI may improve noninvasive estimation of BM origin and support more targeted diagnostic evaluation in clinical radiology.

title: Unprecedented OS with the addition of tarlatamab to first-line maintenance therapy for ES-SCLC.
authors: Killock D

title: Explainable machine learning for predicting grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events in resectable non-small cell lung cancer receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy: predominant contribution of hematologic toxicity.
authors: Zhi FH, Zhang Y, Ge T et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy improves outcomes for resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but can cause severe treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). Pretreatment models for predicting grade ≥3 TRAEs during neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy remain limited. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an explainable machine learning model for predicting grade ≥3 TRAEs in patients with resectable NSCLC receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy.
METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included a discovery cohort (n=953) and an independent external validation cohort (n=143). The discovery cohort was stratified into training (n=668) and internal test (n=285) sets. Pretreatment candidates included routine clinical and laboratory variables and first-cycle treatment characteristics. Stability-oriented Boruta selection was used for variable selection, followed by variance inflation factor (VIF) assessment. Eight machine learning (ML) algorithms were tuned using 10-fold cross-validation in the training set. Discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and explanations based on SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were evaluated. Secondary analyses assessed hematologic, nonhematologic, and immune-related adverse event (irAE) endpoints.
RESULTS: Grade ≥3 TRAEs occurred in 496 of 1,096 patients (45.3%); 464 patients (42.3%) experienced grade ≥3 hematologic toxicity, and 446 (89.9% of patients with grade ≥3 TRAEs) reached the composite endpoint exclusively because of hematologic events. The final random forest model incorporating 12 pretreatment predictors achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.782 and 0.742 in the internal test and external validation cohorts, respectively. When the locked overall-TRAE model was applied to toxicity subtypes, discrimination was maintained for grade ≥3 hematologic toxicity (AUCs, 0.764 and 0.732) but was substantially weaker for grade ≥3 nonhematologic toxicity (0.638 and 0.631) and any-grade irAEs (0.435 and 0.535). The hematologic toxicity-specific model achieved AUCs of 0.777 and 0.711 in the internal test and external validation cohorts, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: The pretreatment random forest model showed moderate external discrimination for overall grade ≥3 TRAEs, primarily reflecting hematologic toxicity.

title: Astragalus polysaccharide exerts anti-tumor effects associated with altered TIGIT-CD155 axis expression in Lewis lung carcinoma models.
authors: Wang B, Wang P, Hu Z
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), particularly the use of Astragalus membranaceus (Huangqi), has received increasing attention in the treatment of cancer. Astragalus polysaccharide (APS), the principal bioactive component of Astragalus membranaceus, has demonstrated notable antitumor and immunomodulatory effects. The T cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain (TIGIT)-CD155 (poliovirus receptor) immune checkpoint axis has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer immunotherapy. This study aimed to explore the antitumor effects of APS and elucidate its underlying mechanisms of action, including its role in the TIGIT-CD155 immune checkpoint axis in lung cancer.
METHODS: Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) cells were treated with different concentrations of APS (200, 400, and 800 µg/mL). Cell viability, apoptosis, migration, and invasion were assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assays, flow cytometry, wound healing assays, and transwell assays. Additionally, Western blot analysis was performed to evaluate the protein expression levels of TIGIT, CD155, matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9), focal adhesion kinase (FAK), Bcl-2, and BAX. In vivo experiments were conducted using an LLC mouse model, which was treated with APS and/or the TIGIT inhibitor ociperlimab. Tumor growth, immune cell infiltration, and TIGIT-CD155 expression were subsequently analyzed.
RESULTS: APS significantly inhibited LLC cell proliferation in a dose-dependent manner, with notable effects observed at concentrations ≥200 μg/mL (P<0.05). APS also promoted apoptosis by downregulating Bcl-2 and upregulating BAX expression. Additionally, APS suppressed cell migration and invasion through the downregulation of MMP-9 and FAK proteins. Notably, APS significantly reduced TIGIT and CD155 protein expression in LLC cells (P<0.05). In an LLC mouse model, APS significantly inhibited tumor growth (P<0.05), and combination treatment with APS and a TIGIT inhibitor exerted greater antitumor effects compared with either monotherapy alone (P<0.001). APS also increased CD4+T cell infiltration in the tumor microenvironment while reducing TIGIT and CD155 expression. Further, APS decreased the proportion of TIGIT + CD4 + T cells and TIGIT + regulatory T (Treg) cells in peripheral blood.
CONCLUSIONS: APS exerts significant antitumor effects against lung cancer through multiple mechanisms, including inhibition of cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, as well as induction of apoptosis. Notably, APS modulates the tumor immune microenvironment by regulating the TIGIT-CD155 immune checkpoint axis. These experimental findings support the integration of TCM with modern immunotherapy for lung cancer treatment and provide insights into the scientific basis of the "Peiyuan Guben" (tonifying the source and consolidating the foundation) therapeutic approach in TCM oncology.

title: A tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte-related prognostic signature for lung adenocarcinoma.
authors: Tian K, Zhao X, Du J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) have been reported to be associated with prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Effective prognostic models for LUAD remain limited, and more robust biomarkers for risk stratification are still needed. Effective TILs prognostic models for LUAD remain limited, and this study aims to construct an immune cell typing (ICT) score based on TILs to evaluate the survival risk of LUAD patients.
METHODS: Transcriptome data of LUAD were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and seven Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets. The data were batch corrected before subsequent analysis. The ESTIMATE and CIBERSORT methods were used to calculate the tumor microenvironment-related score and the content of TILs, respectively. Differentially expressed genes were analyzed using the R software. Cluster analysis was performed using the k-means partition clustering method. The ICT score was calculated using principal components analysis. Survival analysis was performed using the Kaplan-Meier (KM) method with overall survival as the endpoint.
RESULTS: The 5- and 10-year survival rates of patients in the high ICT score group were better than those in the low ICT score group (P<0.001). The expression levels of immune checkpoint-related genes, such as CD274, LAG3, CTLA4, and PDCD1, were lower in the high ICT score group. Patients with high ICT scores had lower tumor mutation burden (TMB) (P<0.001). The patients in the high TMB and ICT score group had the preferred survival (P<0.001). ICT scores can distinguish survival in different age, gender, and clinical stage groups (P<0.05), and the 5-year survival rates are better in the high ICT score groups.
CONCLUSIONS: The ICT score model showed potential prognostic value in patients with LUAD. It may complement existing clinical indicators to improve prognostic stratification in LUAD.

title: Immune-related adverse reactions across multiple systems in a non-small cell lung cancer patient induced by immune checkpoint inhibitors: a case report and literature review.
authors: Li J, Wang D, Zheng L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), while overlapping multi-system immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are life-threatening and pose great clinical challenges.
CASE DESCRIPTION: A 74-year-old male patient with stage IIIA lung squamous cell carcinoma developed bilateral ptosis, blurred vision, abnormal thyroid function, elevated muscle enzymes and cardiac biomarkers after two cycles of toripalimab combined with chemotherapy. He was diagnosed with ICI-induced myositis, myocarditis and thyroiditis. ICIs were discontinued immediately. Glucocorticoids, methimazole and levothyroxine were administered sequentially according to disease progression. The patient recovered well and underwent lobectomy successfully.
CONCLUSION: Elderly individuals complicated with pre-existing cardiovascular diseases are susceptible to severe immune-related adverse events. Early identification of overlapping multi-system irAEs, timely drug withdrawal and standardized immunosuppressive therapy are essential. Endocrine-immune-related adverse reactions exhibit dynamic evolution; for instance, thyroid toxicity may progress from a hyperthyroid phase to hypothyroidism, necessitating individualized monitoring and replacement therapy according to different stages of thyroid function.

title: Arginine vasopressin deficiency following pembrolizumab-induced hypophysitis: a case report and review of the literature.
authors: Dold AR, Jeker R, Mark M
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized oncologic therapy by substantially improving survival outcomes in various malignancies. These agents-such as ipilimumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, atezolizumab, and durvalumab-modulate the immune system by inhibiting key checkpoint receptors, including cytotoxic T-lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4), programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1), and programmed cell death ligand 1 (PDL-1), thereby facilitating tumor regression. However, immune modulation frequently triggers immune-related adverse events, which can affect any organ system, particularly the skin, liver, gastrointestinal tract, lung, and endocrine glands. Among the most common endocrine disorders induced by ICIs are thyroid, pituitary, adrenal, and beta-cell dysfunctions. Pituitary dysfunction is most commonly associated with combined CTLA-4 and PD-1/PDL-1 inhibitor regimens. This case report discusses a rare instance of presumed arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D) secondary to pembrolizumab-monotherapy-induced hypophysitis, which was unmasked following glucocorticoid therapy. A 59-year-old male with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma treated with pembrolizumab developed gastrointestinal symptoms and was subsequently diagnosed with toxic colitis. Following the initiation of glucocorticoid therapy, he developed hypernatremia, polyuria, and polydipsia. Further evaluation suggested AVP-D, with rapid symptom resolution under desmopressin. This report underscores the complexity of endocrine disturbances associated with ICIs and the diagnostic challenges associated with glucocorticoid therapy in patients with ICI-related hypophysitis. The occurrence of arginine vasopressin deficiency in the context of pembrolizumab-induced hypophysitis is rare and not well investigated, highlighting the need for further research into the underlying mechanisms and optimal clinical management of these immune-mediated endocrine disorders.

title: Segmental distribution of hepatic steatosis on opportunistic low-dose computed tomography: a Couinaud-based analysis.
authors: Galvis I, Alis J, Salvatore M
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatic steatosis is commonly and incidentally detected on nonenhanced computed tomography (CT) as areas of low attenuation. Hepatic steatosis is recognized as an independent predictor of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM), underscoring the clinical significance of its detection and characterization. Low-dose CT (LDCT) performed for lung cancer screening offers a unique opportunity for opportunistic evaluation of hepatic steatosis. The objective of this study is to measure CT attenuation across all eight Couinaud liver segments in patients with incidentally detected hepatic steatosis on lung cancer screening LDCT, and to identify clinical correlates of steatosis.
METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study evaluated hepatic steatosis among patients who underwent LDCT for lung cancer screening between 2019 and 2024; patients with steatosis and available 1.5 mm soft-tissue reconstructions comprised the analytic cohort for segmental analysis. Steatosis was defined as mean liver attenuation <40 Hounsfield units (HU) on unenhanced CT. Mean CT attenuation (HU) was measured in each Couinaud segment on soft-tissue 1.5 mm unenhanced reconstructions and normalized to intrathoracic tracheal air to reduce interscan variability related to scanner calibration and acquisition parameters. Segmental differences were assessed by repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey-Kramer post-hoc correction. Associations between mean liver HU and clinical variables [age, gender, coronary artery calcification (CAC) score, body mass index, DM] were evaluated using t-tests, and multivariable linear regression.
RESULTS: Among 1,000 patients, steatosis was identified in 79 (7.9%); 68 with available 1.5 mm reconstructions (70.6% male) comprised the analytic cohort. Patients with steatosis were younger (median 61 vs. 63 years, P=0.005) and had higher BMI (mean 32.43 vs. 28.59 kg/m2, P=0.01). Mean liver attenuation was -30.9±30.5 HU (range, -109.2 to +27.6 HU). Segmental attenuation ranged from -27.1±30.8 HU in segment 1 (caudate lobe) to -34.0±30.9 HU in segment 7. Repeated-measures ANOVA demonstrated significant segmental variation (P<0.001); segment 1 showed higher attenuation than segments 3, 4A, 4B, 6, 7, and 8 (all Tukey-adjusted P<0.05), indicating relative caudate sparing. Segments 7 and 8 had the lowest attenuation. Within-patient variability was modest (mean standard deviation: 4.91±1.94 HU), though a subset showed substantial heterogeneity. In multivariable linear regression, older age (β=+0.16/year, P=0.001) and female sex (β=+1.51, P=0.03) were independently associated with higher liver attenuation, while DM was associated with lower attenuation (β=-2.44, P=0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, single-center study, the mean attenuation of segments 7 and 8 combined correlated strongly with whole-liver attenuation and may represent a practical candidate proxy for opportunistic screening. Validation in a larger study is needed before this two-segment measurement approach is adopted for routine use.

title: From mammogram to lung scan: Lessons learned toward an implementation roadmap for integrating breast and lung cancer screening.
